item.title: Refund and Returns Policy
item.dc:creator: hibarri
item.content:encoded:
This is a sample page.

Overview

Our refund and returns policy lasts 30 days. If 30 days have passed since your purchase, we can’t offer you a full refund or exchange.

To be eligible for a return, your item must be unused and in the same condition that you received it. It must also be in the original packaging.

Several types of goods are exempt from being returned. Perishable goods such as food, flowers, newspapers or magazines cannot be returned. We also do not accept products that are intimate or sanitary goods, hazardous materials, or flammable liquids or gases.

Additional non-returnable items:

  • Gift cards
  • Downloadable software products
  • Some health and personal care items

To complete your return, we require a receipt or proof of purchase.

Please do not send your purchase back to the manufacturer.

There are certain situations where only partial refunds are granted:

  • Book with obvious signs of use
  • CD, DVD, VHS tape, software, video game, cassette tape, or vinyl record that has been opened.
  • Any item not in its original condition, is damaged or missing parts for reasons not due to our error.
  • Any item that is returned more than 30 days after delivery

Refunds

Once your return is received and inspected, we will send you an email to notify you that we have received your returned item. We will also notify you of the approval or rejection of your refund.

If you are approved, then your refund will be processed, and a credit will automatically be applied to your credit card or original method of payment, within a certain amount of days.

Late or missing refunds

If you haven’t received a refund yet, first check your bank account again.

Then contact your credit card company, it may take some time before your refund is officially posted.

Next contact your bank. There is often some processing time before a refund is posted.

If you’ve done all of this and you still have not received your refund yet, please contact us at {email address}.

Sale items

Only regular priced items may be refunded. Sale items cannot be refunded.

Exchanges

We only replace items if they are defective or damaged. If you need to exchange it for the same item, send us an email at {email address} and send your item to: {physical address}.

Gifts

If the item was marked as a gift when purchased and shipped directly to you, you’ll receive a gift credit for the value of your return. Once the returned item is received, a gift certificate will be mailed to you.

If the item wasn’t marked as a gift when purchased, or the gift giver had the order shipped to themselves to give to you later, we will send a refund to the gift giver and they will find out about your return.

Shipping returns

To return your product, you should mail your product to: {physical address}.

You will be responsible for paying for your own shipping costs for returning your item. Shipping costs are non-refundable. If you receive a refund, the cost of return shipping will be deducted from your refund.

Depending on where you live, the time it may take for your exchanged product to reach you may vary.

If you are returning more expensive items, you may consider using a trackable shipping service or purchasing shipping insurance. We don’t guarantee that we will receive your returned item.

Need help?

Contact us at {email} for questions related to refunds and returns.

item.title: Sectors
item.dc:creator: hibarri
item.content:encoded:
1. energy
  2. finance
  3. government
  4. logistics
  5. Metals and minerals

energy

Connect with energy producers in the coal industry, crude oil, petrochemicals, wind, solar, and hydrogen spaces. Pioneer the energy transition in high-impact discussions and constructive dialogue.

The Energy Sector is one of the youngest and largest industries in the world, in comparison to other Commodity Sectors. Encompassing a whopping $12 trillion, the Energy Industry stands poised to be one of the most prominent at the International Commodity Summit 2025.

South Africa has a hand full of energy expos, but none of them provide a platform for energy producers to connect directly with the top energy consuming industries right then and there.

Most energy events primarily have component suppliers, contractors, engineers and other service providers with minimal engagement with actual customers.

The ICS2025 is a sector ecosystem event, where all of the top energy consumers are present as both exhibitors and delegates. As one of South Africa’s top energy events, the ICS2025 is set to break national visitor records.

Types of Attending Energy Companies:
  • Oil, Gas and other Petrochemicals
  • Coal and Anthracite Producers
  • Renewable Energy, Wind, Solar, Hydro Power, Hydrogen and More
  • Nuclear Energy Companies
  • New Energy and R&D Stage Developments

We at Hibarri fundamentally understand the interrelatedness and interdependence of the various sectors in the commodity ecosystem. By providing a platform for Energy Producers to meet the largest energy consuming industries (namely Mining, Construction, Logistics, Manufacturing and Agriculture) we also provide a network for them to supply to.

  1. Find major energy consumers with open tenders
  2. Build a network of major consumers and related companies
  3. Build a network of major consumers and related companies
  4. Establish their brand amongst relevant industry players
  5. Learn more about the consumer networks and procedures
  6. Get offtake agreements
  7. Network with transporters to negotiate preferential rates
  8. Have open discussions with financiers for project finance
  9. Meet with policymakers and regulatory bodies
Who will be sourcing energy supply?
  1. Mining Companies
  2. Steel Businesses
  3. Cement Companies
  4. Commercial and Mega Farmers
  5. Fertilizer Producers
  6. Industrial Manufacturing Businesses
  7. Production Line and Packaging Companies
  8. Recycling Businesses
  9. Chemical Companies

The list continues. With ample opportunity to supply these various sectors, the International Commodity Summit offers a platform for networking, leads collection, business card exchanging, direct sales and dealmaking.

Exclusive Energy Events

The Energy Exchange Event is a networking lunch for energy sector participants to connect, share ideas and collaborate.

Naturally, the fossil fuel proponents start debating tirelessly with the renewables proponents, and the rest just enjoy the show! This year, we are aiming for a record breaking leads-generation event full of high-value impact investments into all areas of the energy value chain.

JOIN THE LINKEDIN COMMUNITY

finance

Unlock more working capital, equity partnerships and financial structuring opportunities at the International Commodity Summit. Meet with banks, private equity companies, VC firms, and sovereign wealth funds.

The purpose of Financial Institutions at Commodity Events in Africa

A big part of what we do at the International Commodity Summit is that we invite smelters and foundries to buy raw materials from the mines, refineries from fuel importers, steel fabricators from crude steel makers, and the list goes on.

On both sides of the spectrum, there is an increasing need for specialized supply chain finance, short term revolving loans, equity partnership, asset backed lending, long term finance, mezzanine finance, purchase order funding, invoice discounting, et cetera.

Financial industry involvement at the international commodity summit 2025

The opportunities are endless for finance suppliers looking to enter into new cash intensive markets, associate their brand in the relevant industries, and gather leads for a fresh set of clientele.

In the commodity world, businesses usually need various forms of finance to supply their raw materials to their customers.

This creates an opportunity for financiers to deploy their liquid capital into asset heavy, cash flow positive businesses that need it most.

  1. Banks
  2. Stock Exchanges and Brokers
  3. Private Lenders and Financiers
  4. Private Equity Businesses
  5. Venture Capitalists
  6. Fund Managers
  7. Institutional Investors
  8. Syndication Funds
  9. Funds of Funds Businesses
  10. Treasury Departments
  11. Capital Raising Experts
  12. M&A Businesses and Advisory Companies
Collateral, Assets, and the link between commodities and finance

Due to the long history between commodities, derivatives and stock markets, a sub-industry has formed between banking and commodities.

This industry is responsible for approximately $6 billion of the $100 trillion world economy, and constitutes all forms of finance, and all forms of commodities.

The nature of iron ore and steel and gold is such that the commodity price is not as volatile as something like laptops, and is much more sellable at high speeds into basically any willing buyers market, which makes the commodity serve as an asset in itself, which can be hedged or held as collateral by the financier.

The fact that so many channels exist to sell commodities back into the market means that commodity backed finance is usually safer and more effective than regular product finance.

Mines are expensive asset classes, a well known and widely spoken of fact in the commodity world. Due to the value of the underlying commodities, machinery, equipment and other mining assets, mines serve as a brilliant target for financing and investment activities.

In the case of energy businesses, these are the créme de la créme of target audiences for the banks. Refineries and energy producing companies often come with a large list of leverageable equipment and machinery, and various commercial assets. Banks also enjoy working with energy companies because of the long lifespan of energy production assets and valuable collateral.

The Energy Industry is the largest in the commodity sector, and accounts for almost 4% of the global GDP. Energy sector participants at the International Commodity Summit 2025 include crude oil wells, diesel suppliers, LNG, and renewable suppliers like solar businesses, wind farm developers and hydrogen suppliers. The value of a single wind farm can often exceed $10,000,000 and solar fields are following closely in average Net Asset Value. These cash intensive industries rely on external financiers in order to persist, thus making the banks an integral part of the energy development process.

Beyond mining, farming and energy, a large list of manufacturers are attending the International Commodity Summit to specifically target these industries and their participants. That and use the opportunity to meet people they have already seen before, to close deals and solidify trade partnerships.

As one of the top money events in South Africa, this event can not be missed by anyone wishing to connect with the right audience!

Who to finance at the event
  • Energy Businesses (crude oil, refineries, diesel, LNG, wind and solar power businesses)
  • Logistics Companies (Ports, Rail Facilities, Tank Farms, Warehousing, Packaging and Air Cargo Businesses)
  • Mines (metals, minerals, sand and slate)
  • Chemical Businesses (FERTILIZER mining, water treatment chemicals, mining chemicals)
  • Manufacturers (mining and energy machinery, construction)
  • Construction Commodity Businesses (steel manufacturers, galvanizers, piping and tubing manufacturers)

The International Commodity Summit has established itself as one of the most prestigious finance events in the Southern Hemisphere and continues to bridge the gap between commodities and finance.

government

Develop an extensive network of public institutions and agencies, join discussions that formulate policies, and drive national development by attending the International Commodity Summit 2025.

Ministries

Fundamentally, we understand the importance of Government Private Sector collaboration, and aim to position the ICS2025 as a prominent platform for networking between the relevant parties.

With a strong focus on mining, energy, and logistics, we combine the collective forces that shape economies to boost trade. Banks, investors, financiers, logistics companies, and service providers come together to improve the global commodity trade supply chains, while governments source and secure commodities, opportunities and new investors.

Government Panel Discussions

Due to the nature of Government influence on the private sector, we believe that Government Accountability is a crucial and instrumental way to make an impact in the International Trade landscape.

The International Commodity Summit provides a platform for Governments and Regulatory Bodies to utilize the stage to illuminate new policies, trade agreements, build relationships and to promote FDI opportunities in their countries.

As a result of the panel discussions, business leaders, CEOs, directors and listed companies can all listen in on the thoughts of economists, policymakers, ministers and specialists in order to gain insights into the forces that shape the world as we know it.

Foreign Direct Investment

The ICS2025 provides an opportunity for Governments to display their unique value proposition to multinational businesses, in order to attract foreign direct investment and highly capable, profitable newly incorporated businesses in their economies.

We work with a large list of Government agencies to promote fair and equal opportunities for incorporation in various different jurisdictions.

As a proponent of international trade and multinational businesses, the International Commodity Summit has established itself as one of the foremost platforms for Governments to source FDI and promote their services, top industries and senior most investment packages.

Government Agencies

In working with a large repertoire of Government Promotion Agencies across the various sectors, we have come to find that there is a need for Government Agencies to promote themselves, their services and their countries.

As a result, we have opened up our exhibition spaces to Government Agencies to represent, establish and promote the parts of their company or organization that they need to promote.

Embassies and Consulates

The need for embassies to collaborate with both government bodies and private sector players is more critical than ever. We understand that embassies and consulates play a pivotal role in fostering international relations, promoting trade agreements, and supporting their nationals in foreign countries.

At the International Commodity Summit 2025, embassies are provided with a unique platform to facilitate diplomatic engagements, showcase national strengths and strengthen economic ties.

By participating in ICS2025, embassies can further their mission of supporting national economic interests and fostering global trade partnerships.

Chambers of Commerce and Membership Associations

Membership associations play a crucial role in representing various sectors and industries, advocating for their members, and creating collaborative opportunities for learning, expansion and growth.

Members associations can represent the collective interests of their members in discussions with international stakeholders at the ICS2025. Especially in the field of Government Trade and Resource Discussions, members associations can determine which part of the event will be most valuable for their members to attend.

By attending and endorsing member attendance, they can provide their members with opportunities to connect with industry leaders, potential partners, and investors.

Membership associations are integral to the success of ICS2025, as they bring together diverse voices and facilitate meaningful dialogue that drives industry growth and development.

Lobbyists

The participation of various lobbyists at the Summit underscores our ability to create a bridge between the private and government sectors.

We understand how crucial it is for Governments to have direct lines to the Private Sector to understand their needs, and to fundamentally grasp new strategies that will help the private sector flourish while building global economies, through the administration of effective policies.

Thus, we invite lobbyists to bridge the gap between Governments and Private Businesses, in order to facilitate and promote healthy and speedy implementation of policies that boost economic activity.

logistics

Build a global network of shipping companies, rail businesses, port operators, cargo companies, freight forwarders and more. Unlock global trade.

In the fast-paced world of commodities, efficient logistics is the critical link between production and global markets. At the International Commodity Summit, logistics leaders from across Africa and beyond converge to showcase innovative transportation, warehousing, and supply chain solutions that ensure raw materials and finished products move seamlessly from source to customer.

Which logistics sector participants will attend the summit?
  • Port operators
  • Rail companies
  • Shipping businesses
  • Cargo handling and container businesses
  • Freight forwarders
  • Clearing agents
  • Air cargo companies
  • Distribution points & warehousing

Metals and minerals

Connect with producers and processors of coal, iron ore, manganese, vanadium, PGMs, chrome concentrate, alumina, copper, cobalt, zinc, nickel, and more. Build a network in the mining space.

The recent hype around Africa’s minerals and metals sector has created an increasingly large need for producers to find access to global markets.

While many events promote getting investors, private equity partners and major loans, the International Commodity Summit promotes off-take agreements and actual supply.

The benefits of getting real, qualified off takers are immeasurable for metal and mineral commodity producers. Firstly, banks are willing to provide liquidity against agreements with certain off takers. Secondly, the buyers themselves are often quite happy to engage in prepayments with certain companies.

The benefits for mining, metals and minerals companies attending the international commodity summit 2025 include
  • Access to guaranteed qualified buyers in the procurement divisions of smelters, foundries, steelmakers, power stations, and mega manufacturers
  • Access to bulk supply chains and logistics partners through the logistics hall at the event (maritime, port operations, freight forwarding, road, rail, aviation and more)
  • Access to banks and financiers in the private equity and venture capital space
  • Networking opportunities with other miners and potential strategic partners
  • Energy producer networks and preferential rates for energy supply
  • Equipment, machinery and services at preferential rates with preferential terms
  • Access to Speaking engagements and panel discussions with the top industry leaders globally
Exclusive miners event

With the IC2025 being quite comprehensive, and encompassing the full commodity ecosystem, there is limited time and opportunities for miners to meet other miners. For this reason, we have established a high profile networking event, exclusively designed for miners and related mining companies.

The Miners Association is a light lunch and networking event designed for high level dialogue, engaging conversations and a network building power hour between like-minded individuals from all sides of the mining value chain.

Types of Buyers Attending
  • Power stations
  • Steel manufacturers
  • Foundries
  • Smelters
  • Refineries
  • Construction and Infrastructure Companies
  • Automotive Manufacturers
  • Electronic Device Manufacturers
  • Machinery and Equipment Manufacturers
  • Battery Manufacturers

ICS NEXUS: THE ULTIMATE NETWORKING APP FOR ICS2025

Connect, message, and schedule meetings with fellow attendees, buyers, and exhibitors—directly from your smartphone.

At the International Commodity Summit, networking is key. Our upcoming app is designed to revolutionize the way you connect—offering seamless messaging, meeting scheduling, and real-time updates to ensure you never miss an opportunity to build valuable relationships.

Key Features

  • Networking Made Easy:
  • Instant messaging and communication
  • meeting scheduler
  • Real-time updates and notifications
  • customizable profiles

How to get access

When you purchase a ticket you are automatically registered for the ICS Nexus app. The ICS Nexus app is only available to delegates who have purchased a ticket, sign in information will be shared when you receive your ticket!

item.title: Panel Discussions
item.dc:creator: hibarri
item.content:encoded:
Table of contents

  1. Government
    1. Intergovernmental Discussion
    2. Ministerial Discussion on metals
    3. Ministerial Discussion on metals
    4. South Africa: the country of origin
    5. Ambassadorial colloquium
    6. Ministerial Discussion on Energy
  2. Commodities
    1. future of commodities panel
    2. Billionaire's row
    3. supply chain geopolitics panel
  3. Energy
    1. green energy discussion

Government

Intergovernmental Discussion

The Intergovernmental Summit must urgently confront a perfect storm of global challenges. To navigate this treacherous terrain, the Summit must:

Address sustainable mining needs to feed a rapidly growing demand for critical minerals while mitigating climate change risks.

Disclose a strategy to significantly reduce unemployment rates and alleviate the turmoil ridden labor markets.

Aggressively target the geopolitical instability to publicize a strategy for the global financial architecture to alleviate debt burdens and prevent a global recession.

Is BRICS actually going to launch a new currency, or is it all talk?

Address ineffective monetary policies that are crushing developing nations with crippling debt that threatens to derail commodity trade.

Strategically leverage foreign direct investment to build resilient infrastructure that supports the efficient and sustainable flow of commodities across borders.

Ministerial Discussion on metals

In this discussion, influential ministers from accross the globe highlight the most vital key trade agreements, sanctions and global trade deals that affect the commodity supply chains globally, and to release disaster prevention strategies related to the anticipated effects of these policies on global trade.

Additionally, these ministers release the key policymaking plans that will directly and indirectly affect commodity production, consumption, supply chains and global trade flows worldwide within the next 12 months.

Which critical metals and minerals will need additional investment and infrastructure development with the world's new transition?

how does monetary policy affect the metal trade, and what can we do better to incentivise mine development?

Which sanctions are slowing trade down? What is the solution?

Which trade agreements promote trade and to what extent? How do we amplify it?

Which trade agreements or strategies can be implemented on a ministerial level to help the private sector access global markets?

Ministerial Discussion on metals

The G20’s future policy discussion focuses on pressing global economic and social challenges relating to the G20. Based on recent G20 summits and ongoing global priorities, the following topics are likely to be featured in future policy discussion panels:

Updates on the global trade war and tariffs.

Military alliance discussion, and critical mineral consumption of the world's militaries.

Strategies for sustained, inclusive, and balanced economic growth in the commodity sectors.

Addressing inflation, supply chain disruptions, and geopolitical trade tensions.

Regulation of emerging technologies like cryptocurrencies and artificial intelligence.

Supporting micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) in green transitions.

South Africa: the country of origin

South Africa, a previously silent major player in the global commodities market, stands on the brink of an exciting future.

experts are debating about whether south africa has become the new switzerland of the commodity trading industry, and are swiftly trying to get a piece of mineral rich south african land.

With its rich reserves of precious metals, minerals, and other natural resources, the country has long been a cornerstone of supply chains worldwide.

As we look ahead to an upcoming event spotlighting South Africa's role as a country of origin for commodities, this discussion will explore the emerging trends, opportunities, and challenges shaping the industry.

Ambassadorial colloquium

Various ambassadors and diplomats come together to discuss The role of diplomacy in mitigating disputes and fostering stability in conflict zones as a tool to reduce war and increase trade.

as part of this, they will be Exploring the role of diplomacy in fostering regional alliances, like the African Union or the European Union, for collective action

Ambassadors in this discussion will collectively be Addressing challenges such as trade wars, sanctions, and the impacts of globalization.

The Paris climate accord will have to be discussed, including our current stance and how far we've come since it has been released.

In this discussion, the audience will be allowed to ask questions in a Q&A session to discover more.

Ministerial Discussion on Energy

Access information flow to key policymaking plans that will directly and indirectly affect energy commodity production, consumption, supply chains and global trade flows worldwide within the near future.

which industries will become the largest energy consumers in the next 10-50 years?

Which alternative forms of energy can we consider to power these industries to combat global warming?

how can we promote energy sector investment and development?

are state owned energy enterprises the solution, or can privately owned energy businesses make a substantial impact on globl energy trade systems?

how far are we from a green hydrogen era, and is green hydrogen truly green?

who will be responsible for nuclear energy plants and the policies that regulate them? is nuclear energy clean or dangerous?

Commodities

future of commodities panel

Covering the various interconnected commodity sectors, the Future of Commodities Discussion answers the following questions:

Which commodities are becoming critical to humanity's survival, and can they run out?

Is asteroid mining and space travel a reality that will affect the commodity sectors in the near future at all?

Which commodities will be highest in demand in the next 5 years? As an investor, exploration company, and manufacturer, how can we invest sustainably in those commodities?

At which point will humanoid robots replace humans in critical hand-labor jobs, and how can we prevent mass-unemployment as a result?

What role will banking play in the changing world trade systems?

How will supply chains change in the next 5 years?

Billionaire's row

Billionaires’ Row at the International Commodity Summit 2025 is a unique and exclusive gathering of the most influential figures in the global commodities industry. This elite forum serves as a think tank for billionaires who have built empires in oil, metals, agriculture, and energy markets.

Beyond wealth, these individuals hold unmatched influence over supply chains, pricing trends, and market stability. The discussions at Billionaires’ Row delve into:

Strategies to build empires, economies and strategic partnerships globally.

Principles for successful business development in the commodity sectors. Competition, monopolies, and oligopoly development in the commodity sectors - are they good or bad for economies?

Lobbying and strategies to leverage collective influence to address regulatory frameworks and trade agreements.

Future predictions and economic outlook into exploring new opportunities in emerging markets.

Business as philanthropy - the goodwill effect of entrepreneurship, and reframing the public mentality around billionaire contributions. Strategy discussion around legacy and what we leave behind.

Balancing profitability with environmental, social, and governance priorities.

Strategic insights into inflation, monetary policy and a general economic outlook to promote shifts in the thought processes behind economic development.

supply chain geopolitics panel

Shipping prices have recently skyrocket overnight due to a series of factors causing a massive domino effect that is affecting global inflation and disrupted supply chain ecosystems. The Supply Chain Geopolitics discussion dissects the increasingly complex and volatile landscape shaping and disrupting global trade. The key focus areas of this discussion include:

AI and the Internet created a sudden rapid rate of deglobalization, and e-commerce is powering mass movements accross continents. Will the shipping industry be able to keep up before the oceans are filled with cargo ships?

Are bottlenecks in East Africa and the Suez Canal a serious concern? What are the implications of an unchanged Panama Canal and what volume of global trade flows through these two vital channels?

What is the effect of the Houthi Rebels, pirates and other conflict instigators on shipping?

What supply chain infrastructure will be developed, that serves as enabler of trade globally, and what is the 10 year outlook on these infrastructure developments?

Which monetization strategies will help drive collaboration between producers and logistics businesses operating in the maritime world? How can producers utilize these strategies today?

Energy

green energy discussion

Discovery Bank's Green Energy panel discussion at the International Commodity Summit 2025 brings together industry leaders, policymakers, and innovators to explore the transformative role of renewable energy in the global commodity landscape.

This high-level dialogue will focus on emerging trends, sustainable practices, and the economic opportunities driving the shift towards cleaner energy solutions, under which key questions include:

What are the repercussions of inaction toward renewables for Humanity? Why is renewable energy a relevant discussion? Does renewable energy truly solve the problem? Which alternative energy solutions have been effective or promise to be effective in the past?

Which key economic opportunities are directly intertwined with the need for renewable energy?

Which emerging industries will be born from the demand for renewable energy?

Should carbon credits be taken seriously, and how can these credits be utilized to move toward sustainability, if at all?

Will the growing space exploration industry be relevant toward testing, deployment, research and development related to renewable emergy at all?

What are the next steps for humanity if we want to preserve the integrity and ecology of our planet? Will we make it in time?

item.title: Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)
item.dc:creator: hibarri
item.content:encoded:
What is the International Commodity Summit?

The International Commodity Summit 2025 is a high-level global conference dedicated to the commodity industry, focusing on trade, supply chains, infrastructure, market trends, and investment opportunities. The summit connects decision-makers across the mining, fossil energy, agricultural, construction, and logistics sectors.

When and where is the summit held?

Location: Sandton Convention Centre, Johannesburg, South Africa

Dates: November 18 to 20, 2025

This location places the event at the heart of the African commodities economy, making it a strategic gathering point for professionals worldwide.

Who should attend?

The summit is ideal for:

Commodity exporters and importers

Mining and energy executives

Industrial manufacturers

Infrastructure and logistics providers

Investors, analysts, and fund managers

Government officials and policy makers

Supply chain managers and trade financiers

How can I register for the International Commodity Summit 2025?

You can register online by visiting our ticket registration page.

What ticket options are available?

We offer several ticket tiers to suit your needs:

Delegate ticket

vip delegate ticket

government ticket

Each ticket includes access to sessions, networking tools, and digital resources based on tier.

Are group or corporate bookings available?

Contact us at secretary@internationalcommoditysummit.com to inquire about pricing and group registration.

Can I cancel or transfer my ticket?

Tickets are non-refundable, but you may transfer your ticket to another individual until November 11, 2025. To request a transfer, email secretary@internationalcommoditysummit.com

How can I apply to speak at the summit?

We welcome thought leaders from across the global commodity landscape. Submit your proposal and profile via email ( secretary@internationalcommoditysummit.com ) Deadline for submissions: August 15, 2025.

Where is the summit being hosted?

The event takes place at the Cape town international Convention Centre ( CTICC ) in cape town, South Africa—an internationally recognized venue with world-class amenities and direct access to hotels, transit, and dining.

Is accommodation provided?

While accommodation is not included with your ticket, we have negotiated exclusive hotel information for summit attendees. Visit our reccomended Travel & Hotels page for booking links and rates.

Do I need a visa to attend?

Visa requirements depend on your nationality. South Africa offers visa-free entry to citizens of several countries. For those requiring a visa, we provide official visa invitation letters after you register. Please apply well in advance.

Is parking available?

Yes, secure parking is available on-site at the CTICC for daily or hourly rates.

Is the venue accessible for all participants?

Yes, the Cape town international Convention Centre is fully wheelchair accessible, with elevators, ramps, and designated facilities.

Will live translation be available?

The summit is conducted in English. Live interpretation may be available for specific sessions upon request. Contact us ahead of time if translation services are needed.

Who can I contact for help?

For any questions, technical issues, or assistance with bookings, please email secretary@internationalcommoditysummit.com

Can I attend the summit virtually?

Yes. Our Digital Access Pass allows remote participants to view live sessions, participate in Q&A, and access on-demand recordings through our online event platform.

How do I access the online summit platform?

All digital attendees will receive an access link via email one week prior to the event. Please ensure your registration includes a valid email address.

How can I apply for a press or media pass?

Media professionals and journalists covering the commodity sector are encouraged to apply for a Press Pass. Please email secretary@internationalcommoditysummit.com with your credentials and coverage intent.

Still Have Questions?

We’re here to help. Reach out to our team at secretary@internationalcommoditysummit.com

item.title: Green Energy Conference 2025 – Move Now or Miss the Transition
item.content:encoded:
Africa’s energy landscape is shifting fast. If you delay action, you risk being overshadowed by competitors already forming hydrogen corridors, renewable finance partnerships, and policy advisory teams. Energy Conferences South Africa 2025 in Cape Town brings industry leaders together to do more than talk, it’s where strategies become signed deals. You will find private networks, government roadmaps, and investor capital all in one summit. Decide today to secure your position in Africa’s energy future.

Attend the Energy Summit track at ICS2025 from 17 to 20 November 2025 at CTICC, Cape Town. Delegate, VIP, and Investment passes are available. There’s no replacing involvement

item.content:encoded:

    • ⭐15:00 Networking Break

The Conference, Panels & Speakers

Day 1 - 18 Nov 2026

⭐ 09:00 Badge Collection

Leverage this early networking opportunity while collecting your badge and gift bag as a first mover. Plan your day ahead and make sure to start right on time!

(Day 0 badge collection opens on the 17th of November at 13h00.)

⭐ 09:15 Investor Breakfast Reception

Welcome to the first event of the annual International Commodity Summit - no rushing to your conference seat just yet - everyone gets to meet and greet at this multicommodity investor networking reception. Meet locals and international investors during this hard-to-miss rush hour.

10:00 Welcoming

Welcome to South Africa. Discover the hidden gems, natural resources and mineral wealth beneath our soil. Find the opportunities, discover new insights and unpack exciting topics in this orientation.

10:15 South African Commodity Investment Guide

🔴🟠🟡🟢🔵⚫️

As the prime destination for investment into battery metals, base metals, food, energy and infrastructure, South Africa stands positioned to become the single largest economy in Africa via natural resource exports alone.

Recognized as the most trusted economy in Africa, the country is yet to elaborate upon its reputation for resources, and to make the "Made in South Africa" brand known.

This panel brings together government, industry leaders, and investors to unpack how investors can direct their funds appropriately and safely while navigating the opportunity dense Africa and its Southern landscapes.

11:00 Critical Minerals - War for Resources

🔴🟠

The world is hungry for cobalt, lithium, manganese, graphite, and rare earths. Resource nationalism is looming. Countries are fighting for resource control. Electric vehicles, aviation, steel, construction, robotics, space travel, data centres, solar production. Who earns and who sweats? What’s changing in exploration, licensing, and regulatory frameworks? Where are funds flowing and why? From West Africa’s bauxite to Southern Africa’s lithium belt, we’ll unpack where the money is going and what it means for governments and private players alike. How do we unlock investment and capital solutions in these long-ignored but critical areas?

This panel is essential for miners, engineers, geologists, commodity traders, transporters, ports and ministerial level government officials. This conversation strikes at the heart of the international natural resource future.

.

.

.

⭐ 12:00 Lunch & Networking

13:00 Mining and the Finance Sector

🔴🟠🟡🟢🔵

Which commodities are becoming critical to humanity's survival, and can they run out? Which commodities will be highest in demand in the next 5 years? As an investor, exploration company, and manufacturer, how can we invest sustainably in those commodities? What role will banking play in the changing world trade systems? How will supply chains change in the next 5 years?

The Mining and the Finance Sector panel aims to answer these questions.

.

.

.

14:00 Upstream Oil, Gas & Hydrocarbons

This panel attracts geophysicists, petroleum engineers, geologists, scientists and environmental advocates alike.

What is the net effect of oil & gas versus coal on the environment?

Where is the upstream energy sector heading, and what threatens its survival?

South Africa has oil, why isn't it drilling? What is the solution?

Who decides the price of oil? What is the future of the sector in the next 5-10 years?

Money and Crude - what are the costs of getting into the game?

⭐15:00 Networking Break

item.title: South Africa’s Hibarri: AI Tech-Driven Commodity Trading Platform Transforming Africa's Trade Ecosystem
item.content:encoded:
Cape Town, South Africa, April 2025 - South Africa’s Hibarri, an innovative tech-driven commodity trading platform, is redefining the landscape of commodity trading in South Africa, positioning the nation as the "Switzerland of Africa" in this evolving sector.

Born from the Kruger Commodities trading team, Hibarri provides a streamlined digital solution for sourcing, comparing prices, and transacting commodities. Designed to be efficient and user-friendly, it serves both local producers and global buyers, empowering the South African export market through smart technology and simplified processes.

A Modern Platform for Diverse Commodity Trade

This digital commodity exchange platform delivers a seamless experience for trading a wide range of commodities - from agricultural products to energy resources and metals. With a comprehensive, user-focused database, Hibarri enables clients to find exactly what they need, whether its maize from the Free State or platinum from Rustenburg's mines.

“We are not just a marketplace; we are leading a digital revolution in commodity trading,” said Cherrylee Samson, Vice President of Hibarri.

Samson emphasizes that the platform’s mission is to bridge local commodity producers with international markets, ensuring South Africa’s rich resources are visible and accessible on the world stage.

Empowering South Africa’s Position in Global Commodity Trade

“South Africa boasts one of the most diverse commodity offerings in the world,” added Samson. “Through Hibarri, we’ve successfully positioned ourselves within the commodity and trade industry, driving international interest.”

To extend its influence, Hibarri has announced the launch of South Africa’s first home-grown commodity trade event in Cape Town - the International Commodity Summit (ICS2025). Expected to attract over 2,000 global participants, this landmark commodity summit will facilitate major trade deals, foster strategic networking, and spotlight South Africa as an African trade hub.

Connecting Africa Through Trade and Innovation

“Our goal is to unify all commodity sectors with targeted lead generation strategies and meaningful networking,” Samson said.

As South Africa emerges as one of the largest economies in Africa, Hibarri sees immense potential in strengthening its role as the continent’s trade epicenter. Cape Town’s strategic location, paired with advanced logistics infrastructure and a strong financial services sector, positions the country perfectly for international commodity trading.

Ports like Durban and Cape Town remain vital arteries for export operations, while industries like agriculture and mining reinforce South Africa’s export strength.

Strategic Alignment with AfCFTA and Global Agreements

South Africa’s active participation in the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) further positions it as a gateway to African markets. Supported by preferential trade agreements with the European Union, the United States, and other global partners, the country has laid the foundation to attract foreign investment and establish a global trade network.

This year, with South Africa also hosting the G20 Summit, it is poised to take center stage in global discussions on trade, alliances, and sustainable industry development.

“Our abundant mineral wealth and commitment to green technology make South Africa a compelling commodity trading hub,” said Samson.

Export Growth and Economic Diversification

The country’s recent economic performance has been strong, with exports reaching R812.34 billion in early 2024. Hibarri believes this signals not only a potential trade surplus, but also the successful diversification of South Africa’s economy - crucial for long-term resilience.

As South Africa continues to build upon its strategic trade advantages, Hibarri remains at the forefront, shaping the future of how commodity trade in Africa is conducted.

Connecting Africa’s Commodities with the World

Whether you are sourcing agricultural goods, mining exports, or industrial metals, Hibarri offers smart sourcing, transparent pricing, and secure transactions - all through a scalable, cloud-based platform designed for local and global commodity traders.

Hibarri stays true to its core mission: making commodity trading in South Africa more efficient, transparent, and globally connected than ever before.

Mining Events in South Africa
item.content:encoded:
international commodity summit stands out as one of the TOP 3 choices for mining events in south africa

South Africa is home to world-class mining conferences, exhibitions, trade shows, and commodity expos that attract investors, mining companies, suppliers, and government leaders from across Africa and the globe. From Johannesburg to Cape Town, Durban to Pretoria, South Africa hosts some of the biggest mining events in Africa each year.

Among these, the International Commodity Summit stands out as one of the top mining events in South Africa. This prestigious gathering goes beyond being a standard mining conference. It brings together leaders from the mining, energy, oil and gas, steel, chemicals, geology, logistics, and commodities sectors in one powerful platform.

The recent hype around Africa’s minerals and metals sector has created an increasingly large need for producers to find access to global markets.

While many events promote getting investors, private equity partners and major loans, the International Commodity Summit promotes off-take agreements and actual supply.

The benefits of getting real, qualified off takers are immeasurable for metal and mineral commodity producers. Firstly, banks are willing to provide liquidity against agreements with certain off takers. Secondly, the buyers themselves are often quite happy to engage in prepayments with certain companies.

Mining events in South Africa are not just about networking, they are about utilizing human relationships to unlock tangible and profitable business opportunities, explore new technologies, and access global markets.

Benefits for miners attending the conference

  1. Access to guaranteed qualified buyers in the procurement divisions of smelters, foundries, steelmakers, power stations, and mega manufacturers
  2. Access to bulk supply chains and logistics partners through the logistics hall at the event (maritime, port operations, freight forwarding, road, rail, aviation and more)
  3. Access to banks and financiers in the private equity and venture capital space
  4. Networking opportunities with other miners and potential strategic partners
  5. Energy producer networks and preferential rates for energy supply
  6. Equipment, machinery and services at preferential rates with preferential terms
  7. Access to Speaking engagements and panel discussions with the top industry leaders globally

Unlike many specialized mining expos that focus only on equipment or suppliers, the International Commodity Summit focuses on the future of African commodities, mining investment opportunities, trade flows, and strategic minerals legislation that will shape the next decade.

The global commodity ecosystem relies on more than production and trade; it depends heavily on the platforms where stakeholders meet, exchange knowledge, and forge deals. This is where mining conferences and oil and gas conferences play a vital role. These events serve as the marketplaces of ideas, policies, and investments that keep the commodity value chain moving.

Exclusive Miners Event

With the IC2025 being quite comprehensive, and encompassing the full commodity ecosystem, there is limited time and opportunities for miners to meet other miners. For this reason, we have established a high profile networking event, exclusively designed for miners and related mining companies. 

The Miners Association is a light lunch and networking event designed for high level dialogue, engaging conversations and a network building power hour between like-minded individuals from all sides of the mining value chain.

Types of Buyers We're Inviting

  1. Power stations
  2. Steel manufacturers
  3. Foundries
  4. Smelters
  5. Refineries
  6. Construction and Infrastructure Companies
  7. Automotive Manufacturers
  8. Electronic Device Manufacturers
  9. Machinery and Equipment Manufacturers
  10. Battery Manufacturers

Types of Financiers We're Inviting to the conference

  1. Commercial Banks
  2. Private Equity Firms
  3. Venture Capital Firms
  4. Private Loans Businesses
  5. Purchase Order funding and Invoice Discounting Lenders
  6. Commercial Loan Companies
  7. Dept Advisory Companies, M&A Strategists, Insurers and Capital Raising Experts
  8. Stock Exchanges and Institutional Investors
  9. Major Players in Capital Markets

The Importance of Mining Conferences in South Africa, and the Role of Mining in the Commodity Ecosystem

Mining conferences in South Africa and across Africa act as hubs where governments, producers, investors, and traders converge. Mining is one of the continent’s most powerful economic engines, and its sustainability depends on constant dialogue between policy-makers, financiers, engineers, and international buyers.

Oil and gas conferences occupy an equally critical position in the commodity ecosystem, especially as energy remains the backbone of industrial development. These events bring together exploration companies, refiners, regulators, shipping firms, and investors to address critical problems in the industry ecosystems that sustain them.

In many ways, oil and gas conferences in South Africa set the tone for energy security and influence how other commodities are extracted, transported, and consumed in the country, and as the largest economy in Africa, it also sets the stage for the rest of the continent.

Together, mining conferences and oil and gas conferences form the backbone of the commodity ecosystem. They do not operate in isolation, steel, chemicals, logistics, agriculture, and energy sectors all intersect at gatherings like the International Commodity Summit. The ability to standardize information, create partnerships, and shape investment flows makes them indispensable.

The International Commodity Summit is consistently recognized as a top-tier choice for anyone researching “mining events South Africa”, “South Africa mining conferences”, or “commodity expos in South Africa”. Its unique positioning means it isn’t just about the mining industry, it’s about connecting the entire value chain of Africa’s commodities, from raw materials to finished trade flows.

Whether you are a mining executive, investor, supplier, or policy-maker, the International Commodity Summit gives you unparalleled access to the markets you need.

Sign up to find out who else is attending today!

item.title: Agriculture Events in South Africa
item.content:encoded:
The International Commodity Summit has been recognized as One of the top Agriculture Expos in South Africa

Agricultural commodity supply chains are one of the oldest and most established in the world. With supply and demand factors constantly affecting prices, and traders constantly getting involved as middlemen in the trades, farmers are often left with the lowest amount of profit and highest amount of risk.

When trying to find high quality agricultural events and farming expos in South Africa, the main decision lies in choosing farming events that have other farmers exhibiting, and not just machinery and equipment suppliers. The International Commodity Summit has a concentrated focus on being the top export event in South Africa, with a major focus on agricultural exports.

Why farmers choose the international commodity summit over other agri expos

The International Commodity Summit provides a platform for farmers to:

  1. Get access to procurement divisions of major food producers and FMCG powerhouses
  2. Tap into international markets to supply their produce globally
  3. Build a supply chain and learn how to export internationally
  4. Get access to capital, both in banking and private equity
  5. Meet suppliers and negotiate for better terms
  6. Network, collect leads and do deals on the spot
  7. Learn from thought leaders on stage and meet the top local policymakers in agriculture

Exclusive events for farmers to network

The World Agri Forum Welcome Reception is an exclusive event for farmers to network and meet other top farmers, hosted inside the International Commodity Summit 2025. We know that the International Commodity Summit is quite a large scale, wide reaching event, and for that reason, we have curated a special, concentrated and exclusive event for farmers to connect.

Expect learning, laughter, thought provoking conversations and great music at this once in a lifetime event!

sponsor and exhibitor categories in the agri section

The farming section is divided into 6 major divisions, namely:

  1. Cash Crops
  2. Fruits and Vegetables
  3. Nuts, Seeds, Dried Fruits and Berries
  4. Livestock
  5. Animal Products
  6. Agricultural Inputs
  7. Feeds
  8. Hunting and Safari

And no, there will be no live cows roaming the floors! This is a trade show, where the best in business come to showcase their produce for the world to buy.

Types of Agri Buyers that we invite to the conference

The main focus of the Agricultural Sector participation at the Summit is to help farmers export. As a result, we understand that every agricultural commodity has a different supply chain and a different end buyer. We have a focus on attracting the following top buyers:

  1. Flour Mills
  2. Breweries
  3. Edible Oil Factories
  4. Global Supermarkets (for nuts, fruits and fresh produce, especially Middle Eastern supermarkets where they don't have the climate to grow any of their own food)
  5. Sugar Mills
  6. Ice Cream Companies
  7. Beverage Companies
  8. Coffee Chains
  9. Local Supermarkets
  10. Chips Companies
  11. Chocolate Companies
  12. Nut Butter Companies
  13. Pickled, Packaged and Canned Food Companies
  14. Herb, Spice and Condiment Companies

item.title: Energy Events in South Africa
item.content:encoded:
The International Commodity Summit stands among the top 5 energy conferences in south africa

The Energy Sector is one of the youngest and largest industries in the world. Encompassing a whopping $12 trillion, the Energy Industry stands poised to be one of the most prominent at the International Commodity Summit 2025.

South Africa has a hand full of energy expos, but none of them provide a platform for energy producers to connect directly with the top energy consuming industries right then and there. Most energy events primarily have component suppliers, contractors, engineers and other service providers with minimal engagement with actual customers. 

The ICS2025 is a sector ecosystem event, where all of the top energy consumers are present as both exhibitors and delegates. As one of South Africa's top energy events, the ICS2025 is set to break national visitor records.

South Africa has a hand full of energy expos, but none of them provide a platform for energy producers to connect directly with the top energy consuming industries right then and there. Most energy events primarily have component suppliers, contractors, engineers and other service providers with minimal engagement with actual customers. 

The ICS2025 is a sector ecosystem event, where all of the top energy consumers are present as both exhibitors and delegates. As one of South Africa's top energy events, the ICS2025 is set to break national visitor records.

Types of Attending Energy Companies:

The energy section is divided into New Energy and Fossil Fuels

  1. Oil, Gas and other Petrochemicals
  2. Coal and Anthracite Producers
  3. Renewable Energy, Wind, Solar, Hydro Power, Hydrogen and More
  4. Nuclear Energy Companies
  5. New Energy and R&D Stage Developments

We at the ICS2025 fundamentally understand the interrelatedness and interdependence of the various sectors in the commodity ecosystem. By providing a platform for Energy Producers to meet the largest energy consuming industries (namely Mining, Construction, Logistics, Manufacturing and Agriculture) we also provide a network for them to supply to.

activities at the energy section of the event

As a delegate at the conference, you can expect to:

  1. Find major energy consumers with open tenders
  2. Build a network of major consumers and related companies
  3. Establish their brand amongst relevant industry players
  4. Learn more about the consumer networks and procedures
  5. Get offtake agreements
  6. Network with transporters to negotiate preferential rates
  7. Have open discussions with financiers for project finance

some of the world's largest energy consumers will be sourcing supply at the international commodity summit

  1. Mining Companies
  2. Steel Businesses
  3. Cement Companies
  4. Commercial and Mega Farmers
  5. Fertilizer Producers
  6. Industrial Manufacturing Businesses
  7. Production Line and Packaging Companies
  8. Recycling Businesses
  9. Chemical Companies

The list continues. With ample opportunity to supply these various sectors, the International Commodity Summit offers a platform for networking, leads collection, business card exchanging, direct sales and dealmaking.

Exclusive energy events at the conference

The Energy Exchange Event is a networking lunch for energy sector participants to connect, share ideas and collaborate, without having to sift through the rest of the commodity producers at the conference.

Naturally, the fossil fuel proponents start debating tirelessly with the renewables proponents, and the rest just enjoy the show! This year, we are aiming for a record breaking leads-generation event full of high-value impact investments into all areas of the energy value chain.

item.title: Finance Events in South Africa
item.content:encoded:
the top finance conference in south africa to connect directly with your brand's audience

A big part of what we do at the International Commodity Summit is that we invite smelters and foundries to buy raw materials from the mines, chips manufacturers to buy from the potato farmers, porridge manufacturers to buy from the maize and wheat farmers, and the list goes on.

On both sides of the spectrum, there is an increasing need for specialized supply chain finance, short term revolving loans, equity partnership, asset backed lending, long term finance, mezzanine finance, purchase order funding, invoice discounting, et cetera.

The opportunities are endless for finance suppliers looking to enter into new cash intensive markets, associate their brand in the relevant industries, and gather leads for a fresh set of commercial clientele.

Financial industry participation at the International Commodity SUmmit

In the commodity world, businesses usually need various forms of finance to supply their raw materials to their customers.

This creates an opportunity for financiers to deploy their liquid capital into asset heavy, cash flow positive businesses that need it most.

An opportunity window has opened with the International Commodity Summit 2025, where a large concentrated group of mine owners, mega farmers, mass producers and major manufacturers present themselves to potential buyers, in the hopes of supplying those customers.

Types of Financiers Attending the Event

  1. Banks
  2. Stock Markets and Brokers
  3. Private Lenders and Financiers
  4. Private Equity Businesses
  5. Venture Capitalists
  6. Fund Managers
  7. Institutional Investors
  8. Syndication Funds
  9. Funds of Funds Businesses
  10. Treasury Departments
  11. Capital Raising Experts
  12. M&A Businesses and Advisory Companies

Collateral, assets, and the link between commodities and finance

Due to the long history between commodities, derivatives and stock markets, a sub-industry has formed between banking and commodities. This industry is responsible for approximately $6 billion of the $100 trillion world economy, and constitutes all forms of finance, and all forms of commodities.

The nature of iron ore and steel and gold is such that the commodity price is not as volatile as something like laptops, and is much more sellable at high speeds into basically any willing buyers market, which makes the commodity serve as an asset in itself, which can be hedged or held as collateral by the financier.

The fact that so many channels exist to sell commodities back into the market means that commodity backed finance is usually safer and more effective than regular product finance.

Mines are expensive asset classes, a well known and widely spoken of fact in the commodity world. Due to the value of the underlying commodities, machinery, equipment and other mining assets, mines serve as a brilliant target for financing and investment activities. 

In the case of mega farms, these are the créme de la créme of target audiences for the banks. Mega farms often come with their own silos, storage, processing facilities, a large list of leverageable equipment and machinery, fertile land, various residential assets and often their own mines or other forms of minerals on the farm itself. Banks also enjoy working with farms because of the multi-generational client lifetime value, which often spans well over 100 years.

The Energy Industry is the largest in the commodity sector, and accounts for almost 4% of the global GDP. Energy sector participants at the International Commodity Summit 2025 include crude oil wells, diesel suppliers, LNG, and renewable suppliers like solar businesses, wind farm developers and hydrogen suppliers. The value of a single wind farm can often exceed $10,000,000 and solar fields are following closely in average Net Asset Value. These cash intensive industries rely on external financiers in order to persist, thus making the banks an integral part of the energy development process.

Beyond mining, farming and energy, a large list of manufacturers are attending the International Commodity Summit to specifically target these industries and their participants. That and use the opportunity to meet people they have already seen before, to close deals and solidify trade partnerships.

As one of the biggest concentrations of wealth in a single event in Africa, this event can not be missed by anyone wishing to connect with the right audience!

Who financiers can bank as clients at the conference

Financiers can expect premium access to the best in business in the following sectors:

  1. Energy Businesses (crude oil, refineries, diesel, LNG, wind and solar power businesses)
  2. Logistics Companies (Ports, Rail Facilities, Tank Farms, Warehousing, Packaging and Air Cargo Businesses)
  3. Farms (cash crops, livestock, fresh produce, animal producs)
  4. Mines (metals, minerals, sand and slate)
  5. Chemical Businesses (agricultural inputs such as fertilizer, water treatment chemicals, mining chemicals)
  6. Manufacturers (mining and farming machinery, construction Construct)
  7. Construction Commodity Businesses (steel manufacturers, galvanizers, piping and tubing manufacturers)

Exclusive finance workshop

As part of our offering, an exclusive finance event will occur at the conference where financiers will be able to shake hands with other financiers and learn, shake hands and share information. Locate the Capital Markets session to gain access.

item.title: Logistics Events in South Africa
item.content:encoded:
the top SHIPPING conference in south africa FOR COMMODITY TRANSPORTERS, RAIL Operators and Road Haulage Companies in Africa

A major focus at the International Commodity Summit 2025 is connecting buyers and sellers across Africa’s commodity value chain. In the same way that smelters and foundries source raw materials from mines, and food manufacturers source crops from mega farms, logistics companies are the crucial link ensuring that these commodities actually move - from pit to port, from farm to silo, and from factory to global markets.

At every level, logistics businesses - whether in ports, shipping, rail, warehousing, packaging, tank farms, or air cargo - need access to specialized finance and trade structures. This includes supply chain finance, purchase order funding, invoice discounting, short-term revolving credit, asset-backed lending, mezzanine finance, and long-term capital.

Logistics is the heartbeat of the commodity ecosystem, and the Summit provides an unmatched opportunity for logistics operators to secure finance, associate with their clientele, and shake hands in major deals.

The role of logistics and finance at the ICS

The commodity world cannot function without liquidity. For logistics companies in South Africa, this means building relationships with financiers who understand the capital-intensive nature of freight, warehousing, and port infrastructure. At the Summit, financiers will meet logistics leaders who need to deploy capital into asset-heavy, cash-flow-positive businesses.

Types of Financiers Attending

  1. Banks and trade finance divisions
  2. Private equity funds targeting logistics infrastructure
  3. Venture capital firms supporting supply chain innovation
  4. Stock market brokers and syndication funds
  5. Institutional investors and treasury departments
  6. M&A advisors and capital raising experts

Commodities, collateral, and transport AT COMMODITY EVENTS

Because commodities like iron ore, coal, oil, and grain are globally tradable, they often serve as collateral in finance deals. Logistics companies that store, ship, or distribute these commodities are positioned at the heart of this trade. Ports, silos, railways, and tank farms are long-term, asset-rich investments, making them prime targets for financiers seeking stable returns.

Why this CONFERENCE matters in the shipping and transport industry

As one of the leading shipping events in South Africa, the International Commodity Summit links logistics businesses directly with commodity producers and exporters. Unlike general trade shows, this event is centered on real transactions, where logistics companies secure contracts to move minerals, energy, agricultural products, and manufactured goods across Africa and into global markets.

For professionals searching for logistics events in South Africa, shipping conferences, road haulage expos, rail freight events, or air cargo trade shows, the International Commodity Summit 2025 is one of the most important gatherings of the year.

This conference brings together the full spectrum of commodity transporters, including:

  • Shipping companies and port operators.
  • Road haulage and trucking firms.
  • Rail freight operators and intermodal logistics providers.
  • Air cargo businesses and aviation logistics companies.
  • Warehousing, packaging, and supply chain service providers.

The International Commodity Summit is more than a commodity conference, it is also a major logistics and shipping event in South Africa. The event is designed to connect cargo movers with the industries that depend on them, including mining, agriculture, energy, manufacturing, and chemicals.

South Africa’s role as a gateway to African trade makes logistics and shipping conferences essential. The International Commodity Summit provides a platform for the logistics industry to align with exporters, discuss supply chain bottlenecks, explore infrastructure developments (such as ports, rail corridors, and airports), and position themselves for future trade opportunities.

Opportunities for logistics companies at the international commodity summit

At the summit, logistics handlers can:

  1. Network with exporters who need bulk shipping, container shipping, and breakbulk solutions.
  2. Meet producers requiring road freight and haulage for agricultural products, metals, minerals, and manufactured goods.
  3. Explore opportunities in rail transport and intermodal cargo handling.
  4. Connect with businesses seeking air cargo capacity for high-value and time-sensitive goods.
  5. Position themselves as key players in Africa’s supply chain ecosystem.

Shipping, transport and cargo at the heart of the event

As one of the few events that brings shipping, road, rail, and air cargo companies together in South Africa, the International Commodity Summit offers a concentrated space to showcase capabilities, discuss challenges, and build partnerships. Whether moving bulk commodities from mines to ports, farm produce to silos, or manufactured goods to foreign markets, logistics and transport are the backbone of the commodity world.

item.title: Ministerial Level Government Events in South Africa
item.content:encoded:
a conference Where governments shake hands and change industries

Fundamentally, we understand the importance of Government Private Sector collaboration, and aim to position the International Commodity Summit as a prominent platform for networking between the relevant parties.

In addition, our government clients receive full exclusivity for maximum inter-governmental collaboration, and share the Government VIP Section with industry relevant ministers from all over the world. As a result, each government benefits directly from the diplomatic interaction, trade facilitation and network building opportunities.

With a strong focus on mining, energy, and agriculture, we combine the collective forces that shape economies to boost trade. Banks, investors, financiers, logistics companies, and service providers come together to improve the global commodity trade supply chains, while governments source and secure commodities, opportunities and new investors.

Panel Discussions

Due to the nature of Government influence on the private sector, we believe that Government Accountability is a crucial and instrumental way to make an impact in the International Trade landscape.

The International Commodity Summit provides a platform for Governments to utilize the stage to illuminate new policies, trade agreements, build relationships and to promote FDI opportunities in their countries.

As a result of the panel discussions, business leaders, CEOs, directors and listed companies can all listen in on the thoughts of economists, policymakers, ministers and specialists in order to gain insights into the forces that shape the world as we know it.

Foreign Direct Investment

The ICS2025 provides an opportunity for Governments to display their unique value proposition to multinational businesses, in order to attract foreign direct investment and highly capable, profitable newly incorporated businesses in their economies.

We work with a large list of Government agencies to promote fair and equal opportunities for incorporation in various different jurisdictions.

As a proponent of international trade and multinational businesses, the International Commodity Summit has established itself as one of the foremost platforms for Governments to source FDI and promote their services, top industries and senior most investment packages.

Government Agencies

In working with a large repertoire of Government Promotion Agencies across the various sectors, we have come to find that there is a need for Government Agencies to promote themselves, their services and their countries. As a result, we have opened up our exhibition spaces to Government Agencies to represent, establish and promote the parts of their organization and country that they need to promote.

Embassies and consulates

The need for embassies to collaborate with both government bodies and private sector players is more critical than ever. We understand that embassies and consulates play a pivotal role in fostering international relations, promoting trade agreements, and supporting their nationals in foreign countries.

At the International Commodity Summit, embassies are provided with a unique platform to facilitate diplomatic engagements, showcase national strengths and strengthen economic ties. By participating in ICS, embassies can further their mission of supporting national economic interests and fostering global trade partnerships.

Quasi-governmental organizations and member associations

Membership associations play a crucial role in representing various sectors and industries, advocating for their members, and creating collaborative opportunities for learning, expansion and growth.

Members associations can represent the collective interests of their members in discussions with international stakeholders at the ICS2025. Especially in the field of Government Trade and Resource Discussions, members associations can determine which part of the event will be most valuable for their members to attend.


By attending and endorsing member attendance, they can provide their members with opportunities to connect with industry leaders, potential partners, and investors. Membership associations are integral to the success of International Commodity Summit, as they bring together diverse voices and facilitate meaningful dialogue that drives industry growth and development.

Lobbyists

The participation of various lobbyists at the Summit underscores our ability to create a bridge between the private and government sectors.

We understand how crucial it is for Governments to have direct lines to the Private Sector to understand their needs, and to fundamentally grasp new strategies that will help the private sector flourish while building global economies.

Thus, we invite lobbyists to bridge the gap between Governments and Private Businesses, in order to facilitate and promote healthy and speedy implementation of policies that boost economic activity.

item.content:encoded:
Access African Energy Week here

OIL & GAS, Renewables and the future of energy in africa

For the African commodity executive, African Energy Week is not just another summit - it’s the annual pulse check on how fast the continent is moving from resource-rich to energy-secure. To a trader or CEO in the industry, it is equal parts marketplace, negotiation floor, and geopolitical theatre.

Walking into Cape Town’s venues during AEW, you can feel the tension of competing interests: oil majors defending upstream projects, financiers circling new liquefied natural gas terminals, and renewable developers pushing hard for wind and solar portfolios. The mix is volatile, but for a commodity strategist, it’s precisely this volatility that presents opportunity.

The conference also has a political undercurrent. African governments arrive eager to showcase new licensing rounds or fast-track legislation. For traders, that translates into signals about where to expand presence, or where to tread carefully. The speeches are rehearsed, but the sideline conversations, where CEOs weigh whether Mozambique’s LNG is still bankable or whether Congo’s hydropower can genuinely underpin battery mineral processing, are what make AEW essential.

In the eyes of a commodity trader, AEW is a live forecast. Oil, gas, renewables, hydrogen, and even nuclear ambitions get unpacked in one space. The event is as much about identifying the next price shock as it is about making sure your company has a seat at the negotiation table when Africa’s energy future is written.

item.title: African Energy Indaba
item.content:encoded:
Access the Conference Here.

The Africa Energy Indaba is the continent’s premier energy conference and exhibition, dedicated to driving investment, shaping policy, and advancing innovative energy solutions across Africa . Held annually (most recently scheduled for March 2025 in Cape Town), it is widely recognized as a must-attend event for energy professionals and decision-makers in the energy industry.

Over the years, the Indaba has evolved beyond a conventional conference. It is now a dynamic platform where investors secure deals, governments align policy, and private sector players reveal cutting-edge technologies. From renewable energy to oil and gas, from smart grids to energy storage, AEI covers the full value chain of Africa’s power future. Its specialized forums - including the Energy Projects Dealroom, Women in Energy, EV & Mobility Summit, and the T&D Africa Expo - create unique spaces for targeted discussions and real-world outcomes.

The Indaba’s value lies in its ability to convene the entire ecosystem under one roof. It is the place where a minister of energy can meet a global investor, where a solar startup can pitch to financiers, and where continental utilities can debate strategies with regulators. For Africa, where energy access and infrastructure remain both a challenge and an opportunity, AEI is more than a gathering — it is a catalyst.

African Energy Indaba collaborates with the International Commodity Summit

This year, the International Commodity Summit (ICS2025) joins forces with the Africa Energy Indaba to align resource markets with the energy economy. The collaboration marks a significant consolidation in Africa’s business events calendar. ICS2025 brings its influence across mining, commodities, and trade, while AEI commands the energy and infrastructure sectors. Together, they form a powerhouse of dialogue and deal-making that connects upstream extraction, downstream energy markets, and cross-sector finance.

The partnership expands opportunities for participants: miners gain access to power sector investors, energy companies reach commodity traders, and financiers can view both markets holistically. It positions South Africa as not just a regional but a global hub where commodities and energy are discussed in the same arena — a synergy few other conferences worldwide can replicate.

The Africa Energy Indaba is not just another item on the calendar. It is driven by a leader who believes in the fraternity and integration of the commodity industries for the better. Where Africa’s energy story is written, by governments, investors, innovators, and communities determined to build a more sustainable future. Its collaboration with the International Commodity Summit amplifies this impact, creating a unique cross-sector forum unmatched anywhere else on the continent. And under the guidance of Liz Hart, the Indaba continues to chart new pathways for Africa’s growth, reminding the world that the future of global energy runs through Africa.

LIZ HART's LEADERSHIP OF THE AFRICAN ENERGY INDABA AND RELATED EVENTS

At the helm of the Africa Energy Indaba is Liz Hart, its Managing Director and driving force. Hart has built AEI into a globally recognized event that consistently delivers measurable outcomes for Africa’s energy sector. Her vision has been to move beyond speeches and panels to create an environment where projects are advanced, partnerships are signed, and investors commit capital.

Under her leadership, AEI has launched innovative side events such as T&D Africa and expanded its Dealroom concept, ensuring the Indaba remains relevant in a rapidly changing sector. She has positioned the Indaba as not only Africa’s most influential energy conference but also as a trusted partner for governments, utilities, and the private sector seeking sustainable growth.

Hart’s ability to influence broader actions across industries reflects her broader vision: that Africa’s energy transformation requires collaboration, investment, and bold leadership. With AEI now linking arms with ICS2025, her stewardship ensures that Africa’s voice in global energy and commodity markets grows louder, stronger, and more unified.
