The energy transition is no longer a prediction. It is active policy. If your company is not represented at ICS2025, it is not part of the conversations defining regional energy flow, project timelines, and ESG benchmarks.

Every green hydrogen partnership, every solar infrastructure rollout, every clean-tech public-private deal will involve stakeholders gathering in Cape Town in November.

The International Commodity Summit 2026 has established itself as one of the most sought-after steel events 2026 in South Africa precisely because it is multi-commodity by design: the program unites mining, metals, logistics, trade, infrastructure, and finance into a single marketplace where steel is positioned alongside iron ore, aluminium, copper, and critical minerals.

That integrated view is what the steel industry needs right now: not just technical debate, but offtake and investment visibility that moves projects forward.

The Number One of Steel Events 2026 can't Compare to ICS2026 as a Steel Mecca

As demand swings with construction, manufacturing, and infrastructure cycles, steel events worldwide often struggle to convert great discussions into commercial outcomes. ICS2026 closes that gap by seating policymakers, financiers, and industrial buyers next to producers and solution providers, turning briefings into term sheets and introductions into supply relationships.

Attending Companies at ICS2026 as one of the top Steel Events 2026 South Africa

ICS’s hallmark is decision-density: focused rooms, senior people, and deal intent. The conference targets ~500 delegates with a majority from metals and adjacent industries, reflecting the broader ICS composition showcased on other tracks (critical minerals, copper, aluminium).

Types of Companies Attending this Crown of Steel Events 2026

Expect a blend of producers, traders, port and rail operators, engineering firms, insurers, and logistics brands, alongside public-sector leaders and capital providers. The curation mirrors the site’s emphasis on cross-value-chain attendance—where mining meets processing, where processing meets transport, and where transport meets buyers - so that conversations naturally resolve into procurement discussions and investment pipelines.

In contrast to smaller steel events 2026 that isolate exploration, processing, or trade, ICS2026 intentionally connects every layer - from iron ore and pellets to DRI/HBI, pig iron, slabs, billets, coils, rebar, plate, and coated products - while bringing in the downstream users whose multi-million-tonne requirements define the real marketplace. That inclusivity is why searches for “metals events Africa,” “steel events 2026,” or “commodity conferences Cape Town” find ICS: it’s the place where a global steel narrative and an African growth story meet on a single, practical stage.

The Last of Steel Conferences 2026 Africa

With a focus on offtake and investment before year-end, ICS positions itself as the final, must-attend entry among steel conferences 2026: a last-mover on the calendar that draws in delegates still transacting - and still building their December pipeline - when other forums wind down. In a cycle defined by decarbonization pressure, energy pricing, CBAM readiness, and supply-chain resilience, the ICS format, policy plus finance plus buyers, turns end-of-year urgency into opportunity.

This is where the steel conversation becomes a boardroom discussion about bankability, logistics friction (rail, ports, power), scrap flows and circularity, and trade access under tightening carbon rules.

Steel Conferences 2026 and Actual Steel Industry Participation

Executives who could spend November purely on travel triage choose ICS because it compresses what usually takes months - market discovery, regulatory alignment, financing angles, and procurement dialogues - into four concentrated days in Cape Town. The timing, the audience, and the offtaker mix together make ICS the conference of consequence among Steel Conferences 2026.

Types of Steel Welcomed at the International Commodity Summit Event

Across the steel value chain:

  • Upstream & raw materials: Iron ore, pellets, DRI/HBI, coking inputs.
  • Primary & semi-finished: Pig iron, slab, billet, bloom.
  • Finished & downstream: Hot-rolled, cold-rolled, galvanized/galvalume, plate, section, rebar, wire rod, tubulars.
  • Enablers: Scrap and recycling systems, energy and decarb solutions (EAF optimization, H₂-DRI), digital/automation, inspection/testing, logistics and port handling.

Steel Industry – a Deeper Look into What is Needed

National strategies (industrial policy, carbon pricing, import safeguards, CBAM) are rapidly reshaping comparative advantage in steel. ICS2026 creates the forum where ministers, CEOs, financiers, and large industrial buyers articulate what will actually be funded, permitted, built, and bought - so that talk translates into mill upgrades, new lines, and long-term supply contracts.

The dialogue spans refining bottlenecks and energy constraints, the economics of scrap, green power sourcing, and the interplay of iron ore quality and steel grades demanded by construction, mobility, and machinery. That breadth mirrors the cross-commodity, policy-meets-capital approach the ICS site emphasizes across panels and tracks.

Beyond the plenaries, ICS runs seminar-grade sessions that are practical by design: H₂-DRI pathways, EAF productivity, yield improvement, refractory and reliability, automation/AI for quality and throughput, full-chain emissions accounting, and ESG reporting aligned to market access.

Crucially, technical teams sit with financiers, policy leads, and procurement heads-so the “how” is discussed alongside the “who pays” and “who buys.” That fusion is what converts seminars into implementation plans rather than notebooks.

The Premier Steel Summit 2026 Africa – International Commodity Summit

The International Commodity Summit works as a catalyst for the steel industry’s next cycle: capital, offtake, information, and supplier access in one place. The Conference, Panels & Speakers

All guests wear colour coded lanyards for industry based business matchmaking. All panels are labeled by industry.

Day 1 - 18 Nov 2025

09:00 Welcoming

09:15 The Country of Origin - South Africa's Mineral Wealth

🔴🟠🟡🟢🔵⚫️

The world runs on energy from South Africa. Energy pours into vehicles made from metals from South Africa. Vehicles drive to homes where dinner was grown in South Africa.

It's time that the world sees the "Made in South Africa" mark in full.

Renowned for our coal, iron ore, wheat, maize and citrus, our chromium and lithium and our fruit-bearing soil - South Africa is a home, a hub, and the world's next biggest commodity destination. As the prime destination for investment into battery metals, base metals, food, energy and infrastructure, South Africa stands positioned to become the single largest economy in Africa via natural resource exports alone.

Recognized as the most trusted economy in Africa, the country is yet to elaborate upon its reputation for resources, and to make the "Made in South Africa" brand known.

This panel brings together government, industry leaders, and investors to unpack how South Africa can position its national brand as a trusted, innovative, and competitive country of origin.

This panel showcases South Africa’s unique strengths as a commodities and investment hub, explores how the Nation can drive trust and premium value in global markets, and examines the country’s role in Africa’s commodity integration into global value chains.

As the first of many high impact discussions, this panel will highlight how public and private sectors can align to amplify South Africa’s commodities and create a future-ready national brand.

Toni Gumede, Office of the CEO, Stakeholder Relations and Social Facilitation Professional Brand South Africa

Stavros Nicolaou Group Senior Executive Aspen Pharmacare , Brand SA Ambassador & BRICS Council

Zanele Sanni, Chief Director Of Export Promotion, DTIC

Nadine Watkins, Managing Editor, Newskoop, Session Chair

10:00 Fossil Fuels vs Renewables Debate

🔴🟠

In this highly anticipated world-shifting discussion, the foremost leaders in Coal Mining and Green Energy Advocacy battle for the trophy - what does the future look like? Black, or Green?

Queen Mokudubete-Manyadu MBA, Executive Market Opportunity Generation Fraser Alexander

Jaye Connolly, Chairman & CEO, RippleNami

Danie Dorling, Sustainability Lead, Moore Infinity, Session Chair

Oliver Johnston, CEO, Solink (Green Energy)

11:00 Future of Commodities

🔴🟠🟡🟢🔵

Which commodities are becoming critical to humanity's survival, and can they run out? Which commodities will be highest in demand in the next 5 years? As an investor, exploration company, and manufacturer, how can we invest sustainably in those commodities? What role will banking play in the changing world trade systems? How will supply chains change in the next 5 years?

Is asteroid mining and space travel a reality that will affect the commodity sectors in the near future at all? At which point will humanoid robots replace humans in critical hand-labor jobs, and how can we prevent mass-unemployment as a result?

The Future of Commodities panel aims to answer these questions.

Anje Kruger, CEO, Hibarri

George Bennett, CEO, Rainbow Rare Earths, PLC

Thea Fourie, Sub-Saharan Economics and Country Risk, S&P Global (Session Chair)

12:00 Lunch & Networking Break

13:00 Minerals of Africa

🔴

The world is hungry for cobalt, lithium, manganese, graphite, and rare earths. Africa has them. But will we set the price or just ship the ore? Electric vehicles, aviation, steel, construction, robotics, space travel, data centres, solar production. Who earns and who sweats? What’s changing in exploration, licensing, and regulatory frameworks? Where are funds flowing and why? From West Africa’s bauxite to Southern Africa’s lithium belt, we’ll unpack where the smart money is going and what it means for governments and private players alike. How do we unlock investment and capital solutions in these long-ignored but critical areas?

This panel is essential for miners, engineers, geologists, commodity traders, transporters, ports and ministerial level government officials. This conversation strikes at the heart of the African future.

Ian Chauke, Acting General Universal Coal

Errol Smart, Independent Consultant, Ex-CEO Orion Minerals PLC

Jaye Connolly Chairman & CEO RippleNami

Tariq Qureshi General Council Minexx

Dr Lawrence Bbosa, Executive Manager Mineral Processing, Mintek Session Chair

14:00 Agriculture and the Finance Sector

🟡🔵

Agriculture is one of South Africa’s most powerful brand ambassadors - feeding the continent and exporting to the world. This panel will explore how South Africa’s agri-sector shapes the “Sourced from South Africa” narrative, from wine and citrus to grain and livestock.

We’ll discuss how sustainable farming, innovation, and food security drive trust with global buyers, and how agriculture positions South Africa as a reliable partner in international trade.

Paul Makube, Senior Agricultural Economist FNB

Anelise Matutu Head of Commodities JSE

Nadine Watkins, Managing Editor Newskoop Session Chair

15:00 Mergers & Acquisitions Panel

🔵

The M&A landscape in the commodities sector is no longer just about scale - it’s about access, influence, and future-proofing. This panel breaks down how dealmaking is shifting in the age of geopolitical tension, capital discipline, ESG mandates, and resource nationalism. Whether it’s upstream mining consolidation, midstream infrastructure takeovers, or downstream integration plays in energy and manufacturing, the game has changed.

This is where the real negotiators gather - investment bankers, legal architects, corporate development leaders, private equity, sovereign wealth funds, and regulators. The room will be filled with people who don’t just talk about deals - they close them.

Zamani Ngidi, Business Unit Manager AON

Ionut Lazar, Principal CRU Market Analysis

Sherri Hayat, Director, Morae

Shawn Duthie, Director Control Risks

Danie Dorling, Sustainability Lead, Moore Infinity, Session Chair

16:00 Networking Break

17:00 Financial Commodity Markets

🟢🔵

Behind every shipment of iron ore, barrel of oil, or tonne of copper is a web of financial instruments, hedge positions, insurance, letters of credit, and risk exposures that dictate how capital flows, contracts are written, and economies are buffered.

The Financial Commodity Markets Panel pulls back the curtain on the mechanics of global commodity finance - futures, options, swaps, indices, ETFs, structured notes, and everything in between. This panel is not about theory - it’s about the structures, policies, and players that move billions in commodity-linked trades every day.

Manqoba Madinane, FX, Commodities Strategist RMB Global Markets

Christo De Wet, Country Manager Luno

Kirill Kirilenko Leading Expert on Metals CRU

Koshiek Karan Founder & CEO BankerX Session Chair

Dr. Philip M Van Rensburg Founder & Tax Rescue Specialist ProGroup Tax Rescue SA

Ntshengedzeni Gilbert Maphula, Acting CEO Export Credit Insurance Agency (ECIC)

18:00 Green Energy Future

🟠

This high-level dialogue brings together industry leaders, policymakers, and innovators to explore the transformative role of renewable energy in the global commodity landscape. It will focus on emerging trends, sustainable practices, and the economic opportunities driving the shift towards cleaner energy solutions, under which key questions include:

What are the repercussions of inaction toward renewables for Humanity? Why is renewable energy a relevant discussion? Does renewable energy truly solve the problem? Which alternative energy solutions have been effective or promise to be effective in the past?

Which key economic opportunities are directly intertwined with the need for renewable energy? Are carbon credits relevant?

John Taylor Head of Large C&I and M&A Yellow Door Energy

Tobias Hobbach Director Valinor Africa

Jaye Connolly Chairman & CEO RippleNami

Samantha Schoeman Manager, Digby Wells Environmental Session Chair

Day 2 - 19 Nov 2025

09:00 Critical Minerals

🔴

The Critical Minerals Discussion dives into the urgent questions shaping corporate strategy around these minerals - who controls them, where they’re found, how they're extracted, and what it will take to secure their supply in an increasingly resource-constrained world. Resource nationalism? Industry value projections?

Critical minerals are the beating heart of the 21st-century economy. Without them, there are no batteries, no EVs, no wind turbines, no semiconductors, no military tech, and no energy transition.

Nick Beukes, Physical Metals Trader AgriSA

George Bennett, CEO Rare Earth Minerals PLC

Stefano Marani, CEO Renergen PLC

Tim George, CEO Pensana PLC

Pieter Scholtz COO Digby Wells

10:00 Disruptive Tech, Robotics & AI

🔵

Disruption is no longer a buzzword - it’s an operational reality in the commodity sector. The Disruptive Tech Panel unpacks the breakthroughs that are transforming how we explore, extract, process, trade, finance, and move commodities. This is a real-world look at what’s already being implemented, what’s failing, what’s scaling, and what’s next.

From geological modeling to predictive maintenance, AI is replacing intuition with precision. What tools are already delivering returns, and where are the gaps? How are companies integrating ML into legacy systems? Real-time mirroring of mines, plants, and pipelines is helping firms simulate stress, failure, and efficiency. How accurate are these models? What’s the cost of implementation, and how scalable are they?

Jay Van Zyl, Founder Ecosystem.ai

Ryan Blumenow, Director Ai.tuning

Pierre Van Helden, Founder FiveWest

Riedwaan Bassadien, Principal Cloud & AI Specialist, Microsoft

Donald Valoyi, Founder & CEO, Zulzi, Session Chair

11:00 Capital Markets in Commodities

🟢🔵

Commodities are deeply intertwined with global capital markets - and that connection is only tightening. The Capital Markets in Commodities Panel explores how financial structures, capital flows, debt markets, equity issuance, and structured products are evolving to support the next phase of growth, infrastructure, and innovation in the global resource economy.

This is the session where financiers, CFOs, exchanges, fund managers, and sovereign risk assessors speak openly about the balance between capital access and market volatility - and where the next wave of funding will come from.

Hirander Misra, Chairman & CEO GMEX Group & Zero13

Remi Burdairon, Chief Investment Officer, Kessner Capital Management

Shawn Duthie, Director Control Risks Session Chair

12:00 Lunch & Networking Break

13:00 World Economic Outlook

⚫️

The world economy is at an inflection point. Rising geopolitical tensions between East and West, a crude oil war, shifting shipping routes, rapid AI disruption, and the urgency of Net Zero climate transition goals are rewriting the rules of trade and investment.

This panel brings together leading economists and market strategists to examine the forces shaping global growth, capital flows, and commodity demand. From inflation and interest rate cycles to emerging market resilience and the future of globalization, we’ll unpack what lies ahead for businesses, investors, and policymakers in the decade to come.

Zaynab Hoosen, Senior Africa Analyst & Chief of Staff Pangea Risk

Dr Rutendo Hwindingwi, CEO & Founder of Tribe Africa Advisory

Hirander Misra, Chairman & CEO GMEX Group & Zero13

Thea Fourie, Sub-Saharan Economics and Country Risk, S&P Global (Session Chair)

Kalnisha Singh Founding Director KD Strategies

14:00 Oil, Gas & Petrochemicals

🟠

The Oil, Gas & Petrochemicals Panel offers a deep-dive into a sector in transition. As energy security, decarbonization mandates, and shifting global demand redefine how hydrocarbon resources are explored, produced, traded, and consumed, this panel will bring together regional NOCs, international majors, petrochemical giants, pipeline infrastructure leaders, carbon market specialists, and policy architects to confront the hard questions facing the industry.

Joe Amadi-Echendu, Chair, Board of Directors of the International Society of Engineering
Asset Management

Adrian Strydom CEO South African Oil and Gas Association

Unathi Sonti, Chairperson Maritime Business Chamber

Oliver Onyekweli Partner McKinsey & Company Session Chair

15:00 Marketing in Multinationals

🔵

Marketing inside a multinational isn’t about copy-pasting campaigns across countries - it’s about creating relevance at scale. In this panel, we’ll dive into how the best global brands strike the balance between consistency and local nuance, how they translate storytelling into measurable impact, and how they leverage data, culture, and customer insight to build trust in every market they enter. Expect candid insights into what actually works (and what doesn’t) when you’re tasked with protecting a global brand while driving growth in an environment where consumer expectations change faster than quarterly reports.

Cherrylee Samson, Co-Founder & CMO Hibarri

Yudhvir Ranchod, Marketing Director, Peach Payments

Dr. Zane Dippenaar, Head of Marketing, IBC Solar

Jolene van Rensburg, MBA, B.Eng Honours, B.Eng Metallurgy, Strategic Partnerships & Growth Manager Africa and Europe, Mineral Technologies

Rehana Rutti Marketing, Events, PR and Brand Specialist, Session Chair

16:00 Networking Break

17:00 Investment & VC Future

🔵

The future of commodities is being reshaped not just by extraction and trade, but by innovation - and that innovation needs capital. The Investment & VC Future Panel explores how investment thinking is evolving across public markets, private equity, and venture capital in response to the rising intersection of commodities, climate, infrastructure, and deep tech.

This is the session where asset allocators, visionary founders, and strategic LPs unpack the capital stack behind tomorrow’s breakthroughs - from mineral traceability startups to hydrogen infrastructure, mining automation, energy storage, and green industrial manufacturing.

Janade Du Plessis, Managing Partner Africa Launch Ventures

Anje Kruger, CEO Hibarri & International Commodity Summit

Day 3 - 20 Nov 2025

10:00 Hydrogen Economy

🟠

Hydrogen is being billed as the missing link in the energy transition - but how close are we to scaling it into a true global economy?

This panel unpacks the opportunities and obstacles shaping hydrogen’s future: from green hydrogen production and infrastructure build-out to storage, transport, and end-use in heavy industry, shipping, and power.

We’ll examine whether hydrogen can deliver on its promise of decarbonization at scale, who is financing the rollout, and what it will take for hydrogen to move from pilot projects to a cornerstone of the global energy system.

Prisca Mayumbelo, Business Development Officer, City of Windhoek

Mlibo Yokwe Senior Business Development Manager HDF Energy (PLC)

Dean Oliver, Matiere News, Business Development Manager Session Chair

The Networking Continues!

We won't keep you any longer, go make some friends!

item.title: Coal Events South Africa 2026 | Top Coal Conference ICS at Sandton Convention Center
item.content:encoded:
Discover the top coal events South Africa has to offer in 2026. The International Commodity Summit (ICS) at Sandton Convention Cenrter is the premier gathering for mining leaders, financiers, and global buyers. Join us Nov 18-19.

ICS2026 amongst the top coal Events South Africa

South Africa's coal industry commands global attention, a fact underscored by the high-impact coal events South Africa regularly hosts. These gatherings highlight the commodity's strategic role in energy, exports, and economic policy, bringing together mining leaders, power generators, financiers, and technology innovators to discuss the energy transition, supply chain resilience, and investment trends

As one of the world’s most important coal producers, with exports fueling markets in India, China, and Europe, South Africa's events are crucial. In 2026, the most significant of these coal events South Africa will host is the International Commodity Summit (ICS 2026), scheduled for 18-19 November at the Sandton Convention Centre (SCC). Unlike traditional mining expos, ICS provides a unique platform that unites the entire coal supply chain - from miners and transporters to power utilities, financiers, and international traders.

What elevates ICS above other coal events South Africa is the unparalleled caliber of decision-makers it attracts. Chief executives, COOs, and senior strategists from the country’s largest coal producers will be in attendance, alongside board-level representatives from ferroalloy and chrome exporters. Their presence is a testament to coal’s enduring significance. These leaders use the summit to secure offtake agreements, negotiate rail access, and explore joint ventures with international partners. For investors and traders, ICS is a rare opportunity to engage with the individuals shaping the future of coal supply in Southern Africa.

What Sets This Apart from Other Coal Events South Africa

What makes ICS unique among coal events South Africa is its comprehensive visibility across the entire coal value chain. Delegates will include:

  • Producers: Major coal mining companies showcasing export strategies and capacity.
  • Power Stations & Utilities: Key players discussing coal’s role in domestic energy security.
  • Transport & Logistics Providers: Experts from rail, trucking, and port authorities like the Richards Bay Coal Terminal.
  • International Buyers & Offtakers: Delegates from Asia and Europe seeking long-term supply contracts.
  • Financiers & Policy Leaders: Discussions on project funding, clean coal tech, and coal's place in Africa’s just energy transition.

This integrated format allows participants to network across the full coal ecosystem, not just within silos. The international dimension is critical; Asian buyers will confirm long-term contracts, while European delegates will engage on how South Africa’s industry aligns with global carbon commitments. This makes ICS not just another coal event in South Africa, but a vital bridge between African producers and the world’s largest energy-consuming economies.

Coal events South Africa, coal conferences 2026, coal events cape town, and the Sandton Convention Center, 18-19 November 2026.

The Landscape of Top Coal Events

Other coal events South Africa, such as the Coal Africa Expo or McCloskey’s Southern African Coal Conference, offer valuable technical insights. ICS complements them by providing a cross-commodity platform where coal is discussed in relation to chrome, ferroalloys, base metals, and energy policy. This offers coal producers greater exposure to investors active in broader mining and infrastructure financing, demonstrating their relevance within Africa’s entire commodity supply chain.

ICS 2026 represents a turning point as one of the top coal events south africa, ensuring coal is debated within the larger context of the continent’s energy transition rather than sidelined. It is the one event where trade flows, infrastructure bottlenecks, investment realities, and climate considerations converge. For more context on the industry, you can read the latest report on global coal market trends from the IEA.

Key Discussions at the Premier Coal Event South Africa Offers

The conference program will tackle pressing themes: the future of South Africa’s coal exports amid shifting global demand, and the critical issue of infrastructure, particularly the capacity of Transnet’s rail corridors and ports.

Delegates will engage in deep conversations on pricing models, offtake agreements, and how coal producers can adapt their contracts to suit the volatility of international markets. This is what makes the International Commodity Summit 2026 one of the best coal events South Africa has to offer for those looking for diversity. The conference program includes:

  • Export infrastructure bottlenecks - how Transnet’s rail performance and port capacity impact coal flows.
  • International trade outlook - demand shifts in India, Pakistan, and China and the role of South African coal in balancing global markets.
  • Carbon and transition strategies - technologies in cleaner coal processing, carbon capture, and balancing coal’s role with renewable energy.
  • Financing coal in 2026 and beyond - the challenges and opportunities in raising capital for coal projects amid ESG scrutiny.

These discussions ensure that ICS 2026 is more than another coal event South Africa; it is a strategic forum for redefining coal’s future in the context of Africa’s broader mining and energy industries.

As November approaches, it is clear that the International Commodity Summit at SCC will be more than another entry in the calendar of mining events 2026. It will be the place where South Africa’s coal industry, led by its most influential decisionmakers, engages the world in charting a future that balances energy security with transition imperatives. For anyone invested in the coal supply chain - from miners and traders to financiers and policymakers - ICS 2026 is not just an option, it is the defining coal event South Africa has to offer.

The Coal Industry Meets at CTICC

In November 2026, Sandton will become the focal point of coal events South Africa when it hosts the International Commodity Summit (ICS 2026). With coal representing nearly 70% of South Africa’s energy mix and a significant portion of its export revenues, ICS will offer a comprehensive coal supply chain program that goes beyond technical discussions. This mining event at SCC will instead focus on trade, infrastructure, financing, and the evolving role of coal in Africa’s economic development.

Another advantage of ICS is its cross-commodity structure. Coal producers and exporters will not only engage with their direct supply chain, but also connect with stakeholders in chrome, ferroalloys, manganese, copper, cobalt, and battery metals. This is particularly valuable for logistics operators and financiers who often serve multiple commodities and seek consolidated deal-making opportunities.

By positioning coal alongside other high-value commodities, ICS transforms from a narrow event into a strategic mining expo South Africa where multi-sector collaboration drives results.

For participants seeking the most influential platform among coal events in South Africa, the International Commodity Summit represents more than a conference. It is a marketplace for investment, a stage for policy, and a networking arena where the future of the coal industry will be debated and defined. As the mining calendar for 2026 builds momentum, ICS stands out as the one gathering that ensures coal remains firmly integrated into Africa’s commodity story.

Sandton hosts the Leading Metals Events 2026

From 18 - 19 November 2026, the Sandton Convention Centre (SCC) will host the International Commodity Summit (ICS), one of the flagship metals events 2026 on the global calendar. The summit is set to draw thousands of delegates representing the full spectrum of the mining and metals supply chain - from copper and cobalt producers to ferroalloy exporters, platinum group metal (PGM) executives, and battery metal investors.

South Africa has long been recognized as the hub of Africa’s mining economy, and Sandton City has become the central meeting point for global stakeholders. By situating ICS at the SCC, the event establishes itself alongside Mining Indaba and African Mining Week as one of the top metals events South Africa will host in 2026.

By placing coal and ferroalloys alongside battery and base metals, ICS ensures that all segments of the mining economy are integrated into a single conversation - a unique feature that no other metals event South Africa 2026 offers.

Metals Events South Africa 2026 - Full Spectrum of Base, Battery, Precious, and PGM Industries

What distinguishes the International Commodity Summit from other metals events Africa is its breadth. While most conferences specialize in a single commodity, ICS provides a multi-sector platform covering:

Base Metals such as copper, aluminium, nickel, zinc, and lead, making this one of the top base metal conferences 2026.

Battery Metals including lithium, manganese, cobalt, and graphite, making this one of the prime battery metals events 2026.

A strong Precious Metals attendance will be present at the event with a focus on gold and silver.

The Platinum Group Metals (PGMs) industry will be discussing the future of platinum, palladium, rhodium, iridium, ruthenium, and osmium.

Ferroalloys and Chrome industry participants are coming through to the International Commodity Summit 2026 in November, critical to stainless steel and infrastructure demand.

A large attendance from the coal industry will be seen throughout the Coal vs Renewable Energy and the business matchmaking lounge at the International Commodity Summit 2026, where they present supply, new mining contracts and beneficiation capabilities required by the metals industry.

While ICS 2026 covers the full range of commodities, coal events South Africa, chrome events, and ferroalloy events are expected to draw particular attention. South Africa remains a global leader in ferrochrome production and a key coal exporter to India, Pakistan, and China. The summit will feature sessions on export bottlenecks at Richards Bay and Durban, strategies for beneficiation, and new financing models for the ferroalloy and coal sectors.

Networking at metals events 2026 - the international commodity summit and volume of metals traders present

One of the defining features of ICS is its emphasis on practical networking. Each delegate badge is color-coded by sector - ensuring that investors, producers, and off-takers in battery metals, base metals, PGMs, or ferroalloys can immediately identify the right counterparts. This approach, unique among metals conferences South Africa, reduces wasted time and maximizes direct engagement.

For traders, financiers, and mining companies, ICS is more than another mining event SCC, it is a high-level marketplace where investment partnerships, offtake agreements, and infrastructure deals are initiated.

South Africa’s events calendar is crowded with mining and commodity conferences, but ICS 2026 stands apart as the most integrated and international. It is not just a technical seminar or an industry expo. It is a cross-sector summit where miners, smelters, traders, financiers, and policymakers converge to redefine Africa’s role in global commodity flows.

For anyone searching for the premier metals events 2026 in Santon, the International Commodity Summit is the one to attend. By combining the scale of a global expo with the focus of a strategic conference, ICS offers an unparalleled opportunity to shape the future of the metals industry in South Africa and beyond.

The International Commodity Summit 2026, held at the Sandton Convention Center in Johannesburg from 18 - 19 November, is a top entry on the list of metals events 2026. It is the flagship gathering for the metals industry, where the full commodity spectrum is represented, decision-makers are in attendance, and global trade conversations meet African realities.

Why ICS stands out Among mining events in Africa

The African continent hosts a wide range of mining expos and sector-specific conferences, but ICS 2026 distinguishes itself by combining scale, international presence, and multi-commodity coverage. It is not a niche technical workshop or an isolated trade show. Instead, it is the flagship metals and mining event Africa, uniting decision-makers across industries at the SCC.

item.title: Hydrogen Expo 2026: Africa's Premier Green Energy Event at ICS - Sandton City
item.content:encoded:
The Hydrogen Expo at ICS2026 marks the beginning of Africa’s energy leadership. The continent is not just participating in the global energy transition — it is ready to lead it. With its vast solar and wind resources, Africa is poised to become the final frontier for green hydrogen, and this expo is where that future takes shape.

This is more than an event — it’s the launchpad for a new energy era. Join us 18-19 November 2026 at the Sandton Convention Center, Africa’s premier venue for world-class gatherings, and be part of the movement turning potential into a thriving green hydrogen economy.

Visualize the future: The groundbreaking projects and technologies showcased at Africa's premier hydrogen expo will shape the continent's energy landscape for decades to come.

Why This Hydrogen Expo is Your Unmissable Opportunity

The world is racing to secure clean energy sources, and Africa holds the key. This hydrogen expo is timed at the perfect inflection point, where technological feasibility meets urgent global demand. For investors, this is a first-mover advantage. For developers, it's access to global capital and technology. For governments, it's the blueprint for sustainable economic growth and energy sovereignty. Don't just witness the revolution—define it.

Experience the Entire Hydrogen Universe in One Place

Forge connections that matter and discover solutions that work. Our hydrogen expo is meticulously curated to provide an end-to-end ecosystem:

  • The Project Gallery: Step into the future and experience Africa's most ambitious green hydrogen and ammonia projects through immersive displays, scale models, and direct access to the visionary minds behind them. From the sun-drenched coasts of Namibia to the wind-swept plains of Mauritania, see the map of Africa's energy future redrawn.
  • The Innovation Arena: Get hands-on with the technology powering the revolution. Touch, test, and talk about the latest electrolyzers, breakthrough storage solutions, and cutting-edge transportation logistics with the world's leading original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) and engineers.
  • The Capital Connect Lounge: Innovation requires investment. This exclusive zone is designed for meaningful dialogue between project pioneers and the global financial community—from development banks and private equity giants to venture capitalists actively seeking to fund the next big thing.
  • The Policy Pavilion: Understand the rules of the road. Engage in critical conversations with senior government officials and regulators who are crafting the policies that will enable safe, efficient, and profitable hydrogen production and export.

Who Will You Meet at This Premier Hydrogen Expo?

This is the gathering of the vanguard. If you are a:

  • Project Developer ready to scale,
  • Investor or Financier seeking impactful, high-growth opportunities,
  • Technology Provider with cutting-edge solutions,

  • Policy Maker shaping the future of energy, or an
  • Industrial Offtaker from mining, transportation, or manufacturing seeking clean fuel,

...then you belong here. This is where your next deal, partnership, and breakthrough will happen.

Your Front-Row Seat to the Energy Revolution Awaits

The conversation about Africa's energy future is happening here. The Hydrogen Expo at ICS 2026 is your exclusive passport to the inner circle of one of the most significant economic opportunities of the 21st century. This is where deals are signed, partnerships are forged, and the continent's clean energy timeline is accelerated with purpose and precision. Don’t just observe from the sidelines — step into the room where the future is being actively built by pioneers, innovators, and decision-makers shaping tomorrow.

Stop reading about the future - start building it.
Secure your competitive edge. Register now for the Hydrogen Expo at ICS 2026 and claim your place in history.

item.title: Crucial Manganese Conference: Africa's Powerful 2026 Rise in Sandton South Africa
item.content:encoded:
The premier Manganese conference for the global industry is set to define Africa's strategic role in the supply chain this November. As the energy transition accelerates, manganese has become a critical component in EV batteries and steel production, creating unprecedented demand and investment opportunities. Africa, holding a significant portion of the world's reserves and boasting some of the highest-grade deposits, is poised to become a dominant force. For comprehensive data on global mineral reserves and production trends, the U.S. Geological Survey (USGS) Mineral Commodity Summaries provides invaluable insights. The Manganese Conference 2026 track at the International Commodity Summit (ICS) is where this future will be negotiated and built, establishing the continent as the epicenter for manganese innovation and trade.

Scheduled for 18 - 19 November at the Sandton Convention Center in South Africa, this dedicated manganese conference is more than just a series of talks; it's the central nervous system for the global manganese industry. We are moving beyond generic mining discussions to provide a hyper-focused forum for producers, off-takers, logistics experts, and technology innovators. This unique concentration of expertise is what sets this event apart from other mineral-focused gatherings, offering unparalleled access to the key decision-makers driving the market forward.

Why This Manganese Conference is Different

While other events may touch on manganese, the ICS 2026 dedicates an entire stream to its specific opportunities and challenges. This is where you will:

  • Source Reliable Supply: Connect directly with leading manganese miners and exporters from across Africa, including South Africa, Gabon, and Ghana, to secure long-term partnerships and negotiate contracts.
  • Understand Market Dynamics: Gain strategic insights into pricing volatility, global demand forecasts from the steel and battery sectors, and the profound impact of geopolitical shifts on trade routes and supply security.
  • Navigate Logistics & Infrastructure: Address the critical challenges of transporting manganese from mine to market, with practical solutions from top logistics firms, rail corporations, and port authorities who manage bulk commodity exports daily.
  • Explore Beneficiation & Technology: Discover the latest advancements in processing, refining, and the development of high-purity manganese for the battery market, moving beyond raw extraction to higher-value products.

The Critical Questions We Will Address

This manganese conference is built on strategic dialogue. Our sessions are designed to answer the pressing questions keeping industry leaders awake at night:

  2. Battery Supply Chains - Growing EV markets in Europe, the U.S., and Asia are accelerating demand for high-purity manganese sulphate. item.title: Privacy Policy: International Commodity Summit & Events
item.content:encoded:
Privacy Policy: International Commodity Summit & Events

Last Updated: April 9, 2026

1. Introduction

International Commodity Summit ("we," "us," or "our") is committed to protecting the privacy of our delegates, sponsors, and partners. This policy explains how we handle personal information collected through our LinkedIn advertisements and registration for the International Commodity Summit and associated networking events like Commodity Cocktails.

2. Information We Collect

When you interact with our LinkedIn Lead Gen Forms or register for our events, we may collect:

  • Contact Information: Name, professional email address, and phone number.
  • Professional Details: Job title, company name, industry, and LinkedIn profile URL.
  • Event-Specific Data: Dietary requirements (for catering at the Sandton Convention Centre), accessibility needs, and networking preferences.

3. Purpose of Processing

We process your data for the following "Direct Functional Constraints":

  • Event Administration: Processing your registration for the Summit (Nov 18–19) and the Commodity Cocktails (May 27).
  • Communication: Sending logistical updates, venue information, and digital badges.
  • Marketing: Providing information on future commodity summits and relevant industry insights (subject to your opt-in consent).

4. Legal Basis for Processing

  • Consent: By submitting your details via LinkedIn, you provide explicit consent for us to contact you regarding the Summit.
  • Contractual Necessity: We require your data to fulfill your attendance at our events.
  • Legitimate Interest: To improve our event offerings and ensure a high-quality networking experience.

5. Third-Party Sharing & International Transfers

We do not sell your data. However, we may share information with:

  • Service Providers: Such as the Sandton Convention Centre (for security/access) and event management software.
  • International Transfers: As an international summit, your data may be processed on secure servers located outside of South Africa. We ensure these transfers comply with POPIA Section 72 and GDPR standards using Standard Contractual Clauses.

6. Data Retention

We retain your information only as long as necessary to facilitate the events or to comply with South African tax and legal record-keeping requirements (typically 5 years for financial transactions).

7. Your Rights (POPIA & GDPR)

You have the right to:

  • Access: Request a copy of the personal data we hold.
  • Correction: Update inaccurate professional details.
  • Objection/Withdrawal: Opt-out of marketing or withdraw consent for data processing at any time.
  • Deletion: Request that your data be "forgotten" following the conclusion of the summit.

8. Security

We implement industry-standard technical and organizational measures (encryption, firewalls) to protect your data from unauthorized access, particularly during the processing of high-scale contact lists.

9. Contact Us

For any privacy-related inquiries or to exercise your rights, please contact our Information Officer at: Email: secretry@internationalcommoditysummit.com

Address: Century City, Cape Town

This iconic destination combines sophisticated conference facilities with easy access to accommodation, dining, and networking opportunities that extend well beyond the formal programme. The ICS 2026 isn't just another entry on the calendar of metals events South Africa hosts each year. It's a carefully curated gathering designed to maximise value for every participant. Key sectors covered include:

The strength of any conference lies in its attendees. ICS 2026 attracts a powerful cross-section of the global commodity ecosystem:

item.title: Aluminium Conferences 2026 - Fly to this Important Aluminium Event 2026 South Africa (ICS2026)
item.content:encoded:
Fly to Sandton, Johannesburg 18-19 November 2026 for one of the world's leading aluminium conferences 2026 South Africa – the International Commodity Summit 2026 – meet offtakers, investors, banks, suppliers, ministers, leaders and academics.

Table of Contents

Aluminium Events 2026 South Africa – The International Commodity Summit 2026

The aluminium industry is projected to be worth over $400 billion by 2030 – as the world braces for impact, the International Commodity Summit stands ready to propel the industry toward its destiny.

While the aluminium industry centres around casting, smelting, rolling, producing sheets, ingots, billets and manufacturing cars, planes, boats and large structures, it remains deeply interlinked with the steel, metallurgical, alloying, metals and mining industries. For this reason, the International Commodity Summit 2026 stands out as the world's best destination for aluminium conferences 2026 – and has been marked as the world's top aluminium event 2026 Africa by various industry sources.

Consolidation of Metals Industries at ICS2026

The base metals, precious metals, ferrous, non-ferrous, foundry, battery metals, metal mining and platinum group metals industries will all be present at the International Commodity Summit 2026. This makes it the world's preferred aluminium conference 2026 for its refined focus on the metals industry and its ability to connect producers, suppliers and investors with the full value chain.

When professionals across mining, manufacturing, energy, logistics, and finance search for Aluminium Events 2026, they are not simply looking for another industry gathering or a regional trade show. They are searching for a comprehensive platform that combines global scale, serious investment, industrial demand, and policy influence. The International Commodity Summit 2026 offers exactly that, positioning itself as the single most important entry in the global calendar of Aluminium Events 2026.

The Role of Aluminium in the International Metals Industry

The international metals industry is interconnected, and aluminium plays both a standalone and supportive role within it:

  • Aluminium substitutes for steel in automotive manufacturing when weight reduction is crucial
  • It complements copper in power transmission and electrical infrastructure
  • It interacts with alloys in aerospace and defense applications
  • It ties into battery and renewable technologies as part of the broader critical mineral narrative
  • It is found in datacenters powering the AI revolution

These intersections are precisely why aluminium is integrated into the International Commodity Summit 2026 as one of the premier aluminium conferences 2026, as opposed to standalone aluminium events 2026.

The Aluminium Value Chain Relevance at ICS2026

Delegates can agree that attending aluminium conferences 2026 for academic discussions and philosophical debates is besides the point. Trade needs to manifest. Deals need to be made. This is why the International Commodity Summit stands out above all aluminium conferences 2026 – it ensures direct dealmaking.

At ICS, aluminium producers, alumina refiners, smelters, and recyclers do not just meet within their own sector – they sit alongside copper miners, steel manufacturers, battery metals producers, and logistics providers. This creates a cross-pollination environment where knowledge is shared, deals are signed, and value chains are aligned.

The aluminium value chain begins with the extraction of bauxite, primarily in countries like Guinea, Australia, and Brazil. This ore is refined into alumina, which is then smelted into primary aluminium through energy-intensive processes. From there, the chain branches into semi-finished products such as rolled sheets, extrusions, foils, and castings, before finally reaching end-use industries like automotive, construction, packaging, electronics, and renewable energy.

Intersection of Aluminium and the Metals Industry

As governments and industries demand greener supply chains, aluminium's recyclability and its role in lightweighting and renewable energy infrastructure make it central to decarbonization.

Where the aluminium value chain becomes particularly interesting, and commercially powerful, is at its points of intersection with other metals and industries:

  • In alloys, aluminium intersects with magnesium, silicon, and copper to create specialized products for aerospace and automotive
  • In packaging, aluminium competes with steel and plastics, creating opportunities for innovation in sustainability
  • In the energy transition, aluminium intersects with copper in power grids, lithium in battery casings, and steel in renewable energy infrastructure like wind turbines and solar frames

These intersections are not only technical but also commercial: they determine where markets expand, where synergies are built, and where companies can capture new customers.

Connect with Offtakers, Investors and Supply Chain Partners

The reason why aluminium conferences 2026 are necessary is to stimulate investment into the aluminium sector, and to stimulate offtake in order for the sector to grow. The International Commodity Summit specializes in connecting buyers, sellers, investors, financiers and transporters – which is why it is the best aluminium conference 2026 internationally.

Aluminium does not exist in isolation – it is an essential node within a complex international network of ferrous and non-ferrous metals, linking with everything from iron ore to lithium. Its role is not only to meet current industrial needs but also to act as a bridge commodity: a material that enables other supply chains (energy, transport, technology) to function efficiently.

ICS2026: The Big Kahuna of Aluminium Conferences 2026 South Africa

The category of Aluminium Conferences 2026 is crowded with academic gatherings, regional trade association meetings, and technical forums, but none can match the scale, depth, and cross-sectoral impact of the International Commodity Summit. ICS2026 defines itself as more than a conference : it is the global headquarters for aluminium dialogue in 2026.

Panels at ICS2026 cover every pressing issue facing the industry:

  • How energy transition policies will affect aluminium demand
  • How decarbonization of smelting can be achieved at scale

item.title: The Future of Coal: Why Coal Conferences 2026 Lead to the International Commodity Summit
item.content:encoded:
Coal isn't disappearing in 2026: it's transforming. While global energy markets pivot toward renewables, Africa's coal sector remains a cornerstone of energy security, industrial development, and economic stability across the continent. For professionals tracking coal conferences 2026, one event stands above the rest: the International Commodity Summit in Sandton City, Johannesburg. This isn't just another industry gathering. The International Commodity Summit positions itself as Africa's premier platform for coal sector decision-makers, offering unparalleled access to the supply chains, policy frameworks, and investment opportunities shaping the continent's energy future.

Why Coal Still Matters in Africa's Energy Equation

Africa faces a unique energy challenge. The continent holds significant coal reserves: South Africa alone sits on approximately 30 billion tonnes: yet hundreds of millions lack reliable electricity access. Coal-fired power generation continues to provide baseload capacity that intermittent renewables cannot yet replace at scale. Coal conferences 2026 acknowledge this reality. Industry leaders aren't ignoring climate commitments; they're navigating the complex transition period where coal remains essential for:
  • Energy security in nations like South Africa, Zimbabwe, Botswana, and Mozambique
  • Industrial manufacturing requiring consistent, affordable power
  • Export revenues supporting national budgets and infrastructure development
  • Employment across mining communities and related logistics networks
The International Commodity Summit recognizes that Africa's coal conversation differs fundamentally from European or North American narratives. Here, the question isn't whether coal has a role: it's how to optimize that role during a managed energy transition.

Sandton: Africa's Commercial Heart Hosts Its Energy Future

Location matters for industry convening power. The International Commodity Summit strategically anchors itself at Sandton City, Sandton, Johannesburg: the financial and commercial nucleus of Africa's most industrialized economy. Sandton offers coal sector professionals immediate proximity to:
  • Mining houses and coal producers headquartered in Johannesburg
  • Energy regulators including NERSA and government ministries
  • Financial institutions funding coal projects and energy infrastructure
  • Logistics providers managing rail, port, and trucking operations
  • International buyers seeking African thermal and metallurgical coal
This geographic advantage transforms the summit from a theoretical conference into a deal-making environment where off-take agreements, financing structures, and supply contracts take shape in real time.

What Sets the International Commodity Summit Apart

The global conference circuit offers numerous energy conferences in 2026, but few deliver the specific combination of African focus, cross-commodity integration, and commercial orientation that defines the International Commodity Summit.

Integrated Commodity Perspective

Coal doesn't exist in isolation. The summit's cross-commodity structure means coal professionals engage directly with stakeholders from:

These aren't sidebar conversations. They're central to the summit's value proposition, giving attendees insight into policy directions before they become public mandates.

Energy Security and Logistics: The Twin Pillars of Coal's Future

Africa's coal sector faces two defining challenges that will dominate coal conferences 2026: ensuring energy security while optimizing logistics infrastructure.

Energy Security in a Transitioning Landscape

Southern Africa's power crisis isn't theoretical: it's daily reality for millions of businesses and households. Load shedding, grid instability, and insufficient generation capacity create enormous economic drag. Coal-fired power plants, despite their climate implications, represent the fastest path to reliable baseload capacity given current technological and financial constraints. The International Commodity Summit addresses this tension head-on. Sessions explore:
  • Cleaner coal technologies including high-efficiency, low-emissions (HELE) plants
  • Carbon capture and storage pilot projects and commercial viability
  • Blended generation strategies balancing coal with renewables and gas

  • Just transition planning supporting coal-dependent communities through energy shifts
This isn't about ignoring climate commitments: it's about managing energy transition realities in African contexts where energy poverty remains a more immediate crisis than carbon targets.

Coal's value proposition depends entirely on efficient logistics. South Africa's coal exports compete globally against Australian, Indonesian, and Russian suppliers. Domestic coal must reach power plants cost-effectively. Metallurgical coal needs timely port access. The summit brings together the full logistics ecosystem:

Beyond the Conference Floor: Side Events and Strategic Engagement

  • Executive roundtables for senior decision-makers discussing strategic issues

The Continental Perspective: Why African Coal Deserves Its Own Platform

The summit provides space for honest, complex conversations about coal's role in African development that acknowledge:

Countries across the continent are implementing local content requirements that mandate minimum percentages of domestically produced steel in public projects. Positioning for 2026 and Beyond

item.title: Critical Minerals Conferences 2026: Securing the Tech Supply Chain in Sandton
item.content:encoded:
The global race for critical minerals has moved from boardrooms to the front lines of international commerce. Every smartphone, electric vehicle, and wind turbine depends on a supply chain anchored by rare earths, cobalt, and manganese: and in 2026, the conversation about securing that supply chain is happening in Sandton, Johannesburg at the International Commodity Summit. This isn't just another mining conference. This is where tech giants, automotive manufacturers, battery producers, and mineral suppliers converge to forge the deals that will power the next decade of innovation. If your business depends on critical minerals: or if you're looking to secure long-term off-take agreements before your competitors do: this is where you need to be.

Why Critical Minerals Are No Longer Optional

The term "critical minerals" isn't industry jargon: it's a designation that reflects geopolitical urgency. These are the raw materials that nations stockpile, that automakers fight over, and that define whether a country can produce electric vehicles or advanced semiconductors domestically. Rare earth elements like neodymium, dysprosium, and praseodymium are irreplaceable in permanent magnets for EV motors and wind turbines. Cobalt remains the backbone of lithium-ion batteries despite years of research into alternatives. Manganese is quietly emerging as a game-changer in next-generation battery chemistry, offering higher energy density at lower cost. The global demand trajectory is staggering. Electric vehicle production alone is projected to require ten times more critical minerals by 2030 than it did in 2020, according to the International Energy Agency. Renewable energy infrastructure compounds that demand. Governments from Washington to Brussels have declared critical mineral security a strategic imperative, launching financing programs, stockpile initiatives, and supply chain partnerships at an unprecedented scale. For anyone in the tech or automotive supply chain, the question isn't whether to engage with critical minerals sourcing: it's where to establish those relationships before the market tightens further.

Africa's Strategic Position in the Critical Minerals Economy

Africa is not a peripheral player in critical minerals: it's the epicenter of global supply. The Democratic Republic of Congo produces over 70% of the world's cobalt. South Africa hosts the world's largest known manganese reserves, accounting for roughly 75% of identified global resources. Tanzania, Burundi, and South Africa all hold significant rare earth deposits that are only beginning to be fully explored and developed. What sets Africa apart isn't just geology: it's proximity to rapid industrialization, available infrastructure, and a regulatory environment increasingly aligned with international ESG standards. The African Continental Free Trade Area is reducing cross-border friction, making it easier to move refined minerals from mine to port to end user. The International Commodity Summit in Sandton positions attendees at the nexus of this opportunity. Sandton is not just South Africa's financial capital: it's the gateway to the continent's mineral wealth, a place where mine executives, government officials, and global buyers meet on equal footing.

What Makes Sandton the Right Location for Critical Minerals Dealmaking

Hosting a critical minerals conference in Sandton isn't symbolic: it's strategic. Sandton City sits at the heart of Johannesburg's financial district, where mining finance, commodities trading, and industrial partnerships have been forged for over a century. This is where South Africa's mining majors maintain headquarters, where international investors set up African operations, and where deals worth billions of rand are negotiated daily. For international attendees, Sandton offers world-class infrastructure with direct access via OR Tambo International Airport, five-star accommodations within walking distance of the venue, and a business environment that operates seamlessly across time zones. For African delegates, it's the continent's most connected city: a neutral ground where Congolese cobalt producers can meet Tanzanian rare earth explorers and South African manganese refiners without the complexity of navigating multiple visa regimes or logistics challenges. The International Commodity Summit leverages this geography deliberately. The event brings together the entire critical minerals value chain: from exploration geologists to battery manufacturers: in a single venue designed for serious business.

The 2026 Critical Minerals Program at ICS

The critical minerals track at the International Commodity Summit is built around three pillars that reflect the realities of today's supply chain challenges: sourcing, refining, and securing long-term supply. Rare Earths: Unlocking Africa's Untapped Potential While China has dominated rare earth production for decades, Africa's emerging rare earth projects represent the West's best opportunity to diversify supply. The Summit convenes exploration companies, mining operators, and rare earth refiners to discuss joint ventures, off-take agreements, and the technical challenges of bringing new deposits online. Sessions cover everything from processing technology for low-grade ores to navigating export regulations and securing project finance for capital-intensive separation facilities. For buyers, this is the venue to identify producers who can deliver rare earth oxides at the purity levels required for magnet manufacturing: and to lock in supply agreements before competing buyers do. Cobalt: Ethical Sourcing and Supply Security The cobalt supply chain has faced intense scrutiny over artisanal mining practices, child labor concerns, and traceability gaps. The Summit addresses these issues head-on, bringing together industrial-scale cobalt producers, battery manufacturers, and certification bodies to establish frameworks for ethical sourcing. Attendees gain access to cobalt refiners who can demonstrate chain-of-custody documentation, meet Responsible Minerals Initiative standards, and deliver the cobalt sulfate and cobalt hydroxide specifications required for cathode production. For automotive OEMs under pressure to secure ethical cobalt, this is where those partnerships begin. Manganese: The Battery Metal No One's Talking About: Yet Manganese is having a moment. High-purity manganese sulfate is becoming essential in lithium iron manganese phosphate (LFMP) batteries, which offer longer range and faster charging than traditional lithium iron phosphate chemistries. Automotive manufacturers are racing to secure manganese supply, but high-purity production capacity remains limited. The Summit connects manganese miners in South Africa's Kalahari Basin with battery precursor manufacturers and cathode producers who understand the technical specifications required for battery-grade material. Sessions explore the beneficiation gap: the challenge of upgrading South Africa's abundant manganese ore into the high-purity products that command premium pricing.

Who Attends the International Commodity Summit

The International Commodity Summit isn't a general-interest mining show: it's a targeted gathering of decision-makers who control critical minerals supply and demand. The attendee list includes:
  • Battery manufacturers and cathode producers seeking direct relationships with mineral suppliers
  • Automotive OEMs and Tier 1 suppliers building secure critical mineral supply chains
  • Mining companies and exploration juniors ready to present projects to potential off-takers and investors
  • Government officials and trade representatives from mineral-rich African nations and mineral-importing countries
  • Investment banks, private equity firms, and project financiers evaluating critical minerals opportunities
  • Trading houses and commodity traders bridging supply and demand across continents
  • Technology providers offering solutions for mineral processing, traceability, and ESG compliance
This isn't passive attendance: it's active dealmaking. The Summit features private meeting rooms, pre-scheduled one-on-one sessions, and dedicated lounges where buyers and sellers can negotiate terms away from the main floor.

Beyond the Conference Floor: Why Sandton Delivers ROI

Flying to South Africa for a conference is an investment: in time, budget, and opportunity cost. The International Commodity Summit justifies that investment by delivering outcomes that remote participation simply cannot replicate. Face-to-face negotiations with African producers build trust in ways that video calls cannot. Walking a potential partner through your quality specifications, discussing payment terms in person, and shaking hands on a term sheet creates relationships that endure through market volatility. Site visit opportunities extend the value beyond the conference itself. Many attendees schedule mine visits to cobalt operations in the DRC, manganese facilities in the Northern Cape, or rare earth exploration sites in the Bushveld Complex before or after the Summit, turning a conference trip into a comprehensive sourcing mission. Regulatory insights from on-the-ground experts help international buyers navigate the complexities of African mineral export regulations, beneficiation requirements, and Black Economic Empowerment (BEE) considerations that can make or break a deal.

Securing Your Supply Chain Starts in Sandton

The global energy transition isn't slowing down, and neither is the demand for critical minerals. The companies that secure reliable, ethical, and competitively priced sources of rare earths, cobalt, and manganese in 2026 will have a decisive advantage over competitors still scrambling for supply in 2027 and beyond. The International Commodity Summit at Sandton City, Johannesburg is where that security begins. It's where African supply meets global demand, where relationships are forged that outlast individual transactions, and where the future of the tech and automotive supply chain takes shape. For anyone serious about critical minerals sourcing, this isn't an optional event: it's the event. The question isn't whether to attend, but whether you can afford not to. Visit the International Commodity Summit to secure your place at Africa's premier critical minerals gathering.

item.title: Precious Metals Conferences 2026: Gold and PGM Leadership at the International Commodity Summit
item.content:encoded:
When it comes to precious metals conferences in 2026, the circuit is crowded. Events in Sorrento, Beaver Creek, Zurich, and Orlando will draw the usual mix of traders, refiners, and investors discussing price movements and market sentiment. But if you're looking for something fundamentally different: direct access to the world's platinum group metals (PGMs) powerhouse and Africa's gold supply chain: there's only one event that puts you at the epicenter of production rather than speculation. Gold production in South Africa may have declined from its historical peak, but the country remains a top-10 global producer and serves as the financial and logistical hub for gold operations across the broader Southern African region. The conference agenda reflects this integrated approach, with dedicated tracks for:

item.title: Maize & Corn Conferences 2026: Elevating African Agriculture Beyond Gulfoods
item.content:encoded:
Maize isn't just a crop: it's the foundation of food security for over 300 million Africans, the backbone of livestock industries across continents, and a $75 billion global commodity market that's only growing. Yet when it comes to conferences dedicated to the maize and corn value chain, the industry has settled for events that treat agriculture like a sideshow to consumer food products. The International Commodity Summit, convening at Sandton City, Sandton, Johannesburg throughout 2026, is changing that narrative entirely. This isn't a trade show where maize competes for attention with spice displays and beverage launches. This is where serious farmers, agribusiness executives, commodity traders, and agricultural finance leaders gather to forge deals, secure off-take agreements, and shape policy that moves millions of tons of grain across borders.

Why Traditional Agriculture Conferences Miss the Mark

For years, the agricultural sector has made the pilgrimage to events like Gulfoods in Dubai: massive consumer food exhibitions where the focus skews heavily toward retail, hospitality, and finished products. Walk the floor at Gulfoods and you'll find impressive displays of packaged goods, celebrity chef demonstrations, and innovation zones centered on consumer trends. What you won't find is the kind of high-stakes, deal-driven environment that actual commodity producers and buyers need. The maize farmer managing 5,000 hectares in Zambia isn't there to sample artisanal popcorn. The grain trader securing container shipments to East Asia doesn't need a cooking demonstration. The agri-finance executive structuring a $50 million warehouse receipt financing deal can't waste time navigating a consumer-focused exhibition hall. Gulfoods serves a purpose, but that purpose isn't advancing the serious business of agricultural commodities. It's a B2C event masquerading as a B2B platform, and the maize and corn sector deserves better. The International Commodity Summit strips away the noise and delivers what commodity professionals actually need: direct access to decision-makers, structured deal-making environments, and content that addresses real supply chain challenges rather than consumer marketing trends.

Africa's Maize Powerhouse Demands a Serious Platform

Africa produces over 80 million metric tons of maize annually, with South Africa, Nigeria, Kenya, Tanzania, and Ethiopia leading production. The continent is simultaneously the world's fastest-growing market for maize consumption and a critical exporter to regional and global markets. This dual role: major producer and major consumer: creates unique dynamics that generic international conferences simply don't address. The International Commodity Summit positions attendees at the epicenter of these dynamics. Sandton, Johannesburg isn't just South Africa's financial hub; it's the gateway to a continent where maize cultivation is expanding, yields are improving through technology adoption, and government policy is increasingly focused on food security and agricultural self-sufficiency. Consider what's happening across the maize value chain in Africa right now:
  • Southern African Development Community (SADC) members are harmonizing grain trading standards to facilitate cross-border movement
  • Climate-smart agriculture initiatives are transforming farming practices in response to increasingly unpredictable weather patterns
  • Warehouse receipt financing systems are expanding, giving smallholder farmers access to formal credit markets
  • Value-added processing capacity is growing as countries move beyond raw grain exports
  • Contract farming models are connecting commercial farmers directly with processors and exporters
These aren't trends you discuss in theory at a consumer food show. These are operational realities that require face-to-face negotiation, financing structures, and partnership agreements. The International Commodity Summit creates the environment where these deals actually happen.

Who Attends: The Stakeholders Who Shape the Maize Market

The Sandton Advantage: Why Location Matters

Holding the International Commodity Summit in Sandton, Johannesburg delivers strategic advantages that no other African location can match. Sandton is Africa's richest square mile, home to the headquarters of most major banks, commodity trading firms, and multinational corporations operating on the continent. The concentration of five-star hotels within walking distance means delegates can maximize networking time rather than losing hours in transit. But the real advantage is proximity to Africa's agricultural heartland. South Africa's maize belt is hours away, not continents. The grain silos of the Free State, the commercial farms of Mpumalanga, the research stations developing Africa-specific varieties: all are accessible for serious buyers and partners who want to see operations firsthand before signing agreements. Compare this to flying to Dubai for Gulfoods, where the closest maize field might be 3,000 kilometers away. Beyond Networking: The Deal-Making Infrastructure

The 2026 Timing: Why This Year Matters

Several factors make 2026 a particularly critical year for maize and corn commodity professionals to gather: El Niño Aftermath: The 2024-2025 El Niño weather pattern disrupted production across East and Southern Africa. As the sector recovers and adjusts planting strategies, partnerships and supply agreements need to be restructured. AfCFTA Implementation: The African Continental Free Trade Area is gaining momentum, reducing barriers to intra-African grain trade. Early movers who understand the new framework and establish cross-border relationships will capture disproportionate value. These are valuable platforms with specific regional focuses and technical emphases. What distinguishes the International Commodity Summit is scope and integration. While grain-specific events dive deep into milling technology and post-harvest handling, the International Commodity Summit positions maize within the broader commodity ecosystem. Delegates aren't just maize specialists: they're commodity professionals who understand how grain markets interact with energy, metals, and logistics infrastructure. item.title: Logistics Conferences 2026: The Backbone of Global Trade at the International Commodity Summit
item.content:encoded:
You can mine the best copper, grow the finest avocados, or drill the cleanest uranium, but if you can't move it efficiently from source to market, you've got nothing. Logistics is the backbone of global trade, and in 2026, the most critical conversations about commodity logistics aren't happening in Vegas, Long Beach, or even Dubai. They're happening in Sandton, Johannesburg, at the International Commodity Summit.

Why Africa's Logistics Puzzle Matters to the World

Africa produces a staggering share of the world's commodities: 80% of the world's platinum, 60% of its cobalt, 50% of its manganese, and an agricultural output that feeds millions globally. Yet the continent faces some of the most complex supply chain challenges on the planet, inadequate rail infrastructure, port congestion, cross-border inefficiencies, and unpredictable transport costs that can make or break a deal. Solving Africa's logistics challenges doesn't just benefit Africa, it stabilizes global supply chains. When a lithium shipment is delayed at Durban Port, EV manufacturers in Germany feel it. When avocado exports miss their window due to cold chain failures, European retailers scramble. The world's industries are deeply interconnected with African commodity movement, and the International Commodity Summit is where the miners, farmers, and shippers converge to solve these problems together. This isn't a conference about abstract theory or slideshow presentations. This is where port operators, freight forwarders, mining logistics directors, agricultural exporters, rail executives, and trucking magnates sit down at the same tables to hammer out real solutions to real bottlenecks.

item.title: Iron Ore Conferences 2026: Bridging Supply and Demand in Sandton
item.content:encoded:

Iron ore isn't traded like precious metals. It's a volume game with razor-thin margins, where success hinges on securing rail capacity, negotiating long-term off-take agreements, and timing shipments to match blast furnace schedules on another continent. Traditional mining conferences often treat iron ore as a subcategory. Steel conferences focus downstream without addressing mine-to-mill logistics. The International Commodity Summit breaks this mold by integrating the entire ecosystem:
  • Iron ore producers from Africa, Brazil, and Australia
  • Steel manufacturers from India, China, and the Middle East
  • Bulk logistics operators managing rail, port, and shipping
  • Trading houses arbitraging regional price differentials
  • Infrastructure financiers funding railways and beneficiation plants
  • Government trade delegations pursuing value-addition mandates
This isn't a conference about iron ore in isolation. It's about the system that moves 2 billion tons of material annually, and the commercial relationships that make it profitable.

Location determines participation. Sandton City in Johannesburg sits at the geographic and commercial heart of Africa's mining powerhouse. South Africa produces significant iron ore volumes, yes: but more importantly, it serves as the financial and logistics hub for operations across the continent. When international steel buyers want to source from Mauritania, Liberia, or South Africa itself, they route discussions through Johannesburg. When Brazilian producers need bunker fuel for Capesize vessels heading to Asia, they coordinate through African ports. For a steel manufacturer in Jamshedpur or a trading desk in Shanghai, the value proposition is clear: one trip to Sandton delivers access to African supply, insights into global demand, and face-time with the logistics operators who determine whether your cargo arrives on time.

What Iron Ore Professionals Actually Need from a 2026 Conference

They need multi-year agreements with steel mills that provide revenue certainty for project financing. Capital Allocation: Whether expanding a beneficiation plant, developing a DSO project, or acquiring rail wagons, iron ore ventures require substantial capital.
